identification: School writing exercise (16th-century humanist cursive): alphabets and seven model Latin sentences addressed to the praeceptor ('Manus meae specimen exhibeo praeceptor, mendes a vicijs(?)', 'Praeceptor liceat mihi exire ad reddendam urinam', '... ut adferam cartam, pennas, atra[mentum]', 'Pulsatum est: uisam si libet quid actum oportet', 'Quaeram si libet diaconum, priorem, provincialem vel alium'), copied on both faces; same genre as the 'Formulae petendi quidpiam a praeceptore' of Erasmus-derived phrase books, wording not found in print
note: A research reader read every line of both faces on the image. Face 01r has an alphabet, seven model sentences in a large hand and a second alphabet; face 01v repeats them more densely in another order, with sentence 1 again upside down at the foot. The pupil shows a handwriting sample for correction, asks leave to go out and to fetch paper, pens and ink, answers a bell ('Pulsatum est: uisam si libet quid a[ctum oportet]'; a blind reader read the same opening) and offers to fetch the deacon, prior or provincial, which points to a school in a religious house without naming one. The same requests stand in other words in the section 'Formulae petendi quidpiam a praeceptore' of Hermann Schottenius' Confabulationes tyronum (Lyon 1547), read on MDZ page images; phrase searches in Google Books, the Internet Archive, MDZ and CoMMA found no source for the wording. No human review.

content.title: Writing exercise with model sentences addressed to the praeceptor
content.description: Alphabets and seven model sentences, copied on both faces: 'Manus meae specimen exhibeo praeceptor, mendes a vicijs(?)', 'Praeceptor liceat mihi exire ad purgandum aluum', 'Praeceptor liceat mihi exire ad reddendam urinam', '... ut adferam cartam, pennas, atra[mentum]', 'Pulsatum est: uisam(?) si libet quid actum oportet', 'Campana me ad alia vel domestica quaedam vocat', 'Quaeram si libet diaconum, priorem, provincialem vel alium'.
content.remarks: Same genre as the 'Formulae petendi quidpiam a praeceptore' in H. Schottenius, Confabulationes tyronum (Lyon 1547) and other Erasmus-derived phrase books, in different wording. Source not found. A modern pencil note on 01r appears to name the binding of a 1535 edition as the slip's former host.

identification: German calendar, March-June (central bifolium), in an Alemannic written dialect, with saints' days, day lengths and four columns ('Die erst / ander / dritt / vierd zal') giving the hour of the mean new moon for the four 19-year cycles 1387-1462; of the same general type as the 'Iatromathematisches Hausbuch' calendar, no specific text matched
note: One bifolium of a calendar, one month per page: June and March on one face, April and May on the other, the last two to four days of each month lost. The four columns headed 'Die erst / ander / dritt / vierd zal' give the hour of the mean new moon, counted from midnight, for the years of the cycles 1387-1405, 1406-1424, 1425-1443 and 1444-1462, each year marked by a small red letter a-t: the 68 numeric cells read on the March, May and June pages agree with this cycle assignment: 51 equal the computed mean new moon truncated to the hour and 17 differ by one whole hour (unadjusted differences up to about 1.3 hours; a 0.28-hour shift fitted to the same cells brings all within one hour), and none of the other cycle starts tested fits; one cell has 'kein' (2 June, fourth column), which the computation does not explain. The red column beside them is the traditional golden number. The saints' entries with German epithets and the 27-letter moon column are of the type of the 'Iatromathematisches Hausbuch' calendar (Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 557, fol. 9v and 12v, compared on page images), which has a single cycle with hours and minutes and other saints, so it is of the same general type, not the same text. The spellings ('het', 'frowen', 'glich', 'zechen tusent') are Alemannic and 'Florencie wz erhebt' at 3 April suggests the Upper Rhine, untested against regional calendars; Florian (4 May) and Gotthard (5 May) are also entered, and their bearing on the region was not tested; the years date the tables, not this copy, and no work or witness is matched.

content.title: German calendar, March-June
content.description: One month per page, with saints' entries in German, day lengths, the golden number and four columns headed 'Die erst / ander / dritt / vierd zal' giving the hour of the mean new moon for the 19-year cycles beginning 1387, 1406, 1425 and 1444.
content.remarks: Alemannic written dialect. Of the same general type as the 'Iatromathematisches Hausbuch' calendar, but a different text; no witness matched. The cycle years date the tables, not this copy.

identification: Unidentified Upper German (Bavarian-Austrian) vernacular text, 14th or 15th century, on a parchment spine strip
note: A parchment spine strip, 196/197 x 46/49 mm, keeps the middle of about 30 lines of a late-medieval Bavarian-Austrian German text in a cursive hand, cut on both sides and stained down the centre; the back has binding residue and no script. Few words are secure ('also', 'Kunig', 'wann ez der', '[g]efangen', and on the turn-in at the foot 'sprechen ... Sy waren' and 'recht wol ... vnd ez'), and whether the text is prose or verse written continuously is not settled. A Historienbibel passage on the Egyptian midwives (Merzdorf's edition, OCR text) shares 'sprechen, sy wären', but a line further on it has 'nicht geschaden vnd dienten' where the strip has 'recht wol ... vnd ez'; OCR searches of Ottokar's Österreichische Reimchronik and of the Wernigerode Alexander for the same words and phrase searches in Google Books and the Internet Archive found nothing. The brown-ink 'Mar-/tialis' and the label 'III C/L, 29' name the host volume, and the pencil note on the strip is the shelf number.

content.title: Unidentified Upper German text
content.description: Spine strip with the middle of about 30 lines, cut on both sides; a turn-in at the foot has three better-preserved lines. Legible words include Kunig, wann ez der, [g]efangen, sprechen ... Sy waren, recht wol ... vnd ez.
content.remarks: Bavarian-Austrian spelling, 14th or 15th century. Prose or verse written continuously not settled. Stained down the centre; no connected phrase longer than three words could be read from the published images. Stams_STA_Frg_156_01v has no script. Not identified.

identification: Missal, Proprium de tempore, Paschaltide: Dominica II post Pascha (from Victimae paschali) with its Wednesday and Friday masses and the Dominica III introit (leaf 1); Wednesday and Friday after Dominica IV and Dominica V post Pascha (leaf 2)
note: Two non-consecutive missal leaves, read on the images. Leaf 1 runs from the end of Victimae paschali through Jn 10:11-16, the Offertory, Secret, Communion and Postcommunion of Dominica II, then the Wednesday mass (1 Pt 1:18; Lc 24:1) and Friday mass (Rom 15:14 Certus sum; Mt 9:14), to the Dominica III introit Iubilate; the catalogue's 01r is the leaf's verso. Leaf 2 has Jn 17:11-26 (Wednesday), 1 Thess 5:1 and Jn 13:33 (Friday) and the Dominica V introit, collect and lesson. A second research reader compared 24 lines of 01v with the Missale Pataviense 1498, fol. 85v, on page images, and they agree word for word apart from spelling and a doubled Communion alleluia; the fragment also reads 'venerunt mulieres' in Lc 24:1, as Passau does, and Passau fol. 86r has the same Friday mass. The two Friday lessons agree with a group of 17 uses in Usuarium's tables, from Salzburg, Passau and Chur to Lübeck, Schwerin and Trondheim; this places the book in that group by inference, with no single use claimed, and Brixen differs only in Usuarium's one Brixen witness (the 1493 Brixen print was not checked). No human review.

content.remarks: The catalogue's 01r is the verso of leaf 1.

identification: Fragment of a private German letter (Bavarian-Austrian cursive, late 15th or early 16th century): moral admonitions to a single addressee ('du') about sin, pride and bad company, mentioning 'deiner schwester' and 'das gelt'; writer, addressee, place and date lost
note: The 23 surviving lines on the recto were read on the image: 'verkerett sich warlich pald / wye den deiner schwester geschehen ist', 'den ich hab dirs so trewl(ich) vorgehallten / da du anfängklich hast hin in(?) welle zyhen', 'wye wol ich auch das gelt nimer(?) hab', 'wye oft hab ich dich auch so trewlich gepetten / das du dich ge[...] von yeder geselleschaft', closing 'den gott hatts geschaft / er hatts nitt verpotten ... vnd lass dyr mein(?) predig nitt so ham[...]'. The leaf is cut at the top and right and the text runs off the foot, so salutation, signature and date are lost; a modern pencil note on the blank verso, 'Einband zu II/6 [or II/G] 33 (aus J. 1535)', dates the binding use, not the letter. Phrase searches in Google Books, the Munich digital library and the Internet Archive found no printed or model letter, and the references to the addressee's sister, to money and to earlier warnings speak against one. No outside record was found.

content.title: Private letter
content.description: Moral admonitions to a single addressee about sin, pride and bad company, mentioning 'deiner schwester' and 'das gelt'. Writer, addressee, place and date are lost.

identification: Leaves of a 17th-century Tyrolean court formulary: a model 'Schäz(?) Fürpottzetl' (notice of a valuation court day) of the Stadtrichter ('N.') of Hall, at the suit of Kilgen(?) Mair, burgher and master baker of Hall, naming Thoman Egger, more probably as the Dorfmeister 'zu Rumb(?)' (place unresolved: read Rumb or Stumb by the research reader, possibly Rum near Hall; a blind reader read 'Stamm[.]') who serves the notice than as the debtor, and an innkeeper there read 'Vinckl(?)', for 200 fl. capital, court day 17 November, dated Hall 1 November 16[5]4; with two blank model forms 'Forma aines 14 tägigen Verschaffts' of a Pfleger, the second naming the same place
note: Item 230-4r is read on the image: 'N. Stattrichter' of Hall, on the petition of 'Kilgen(?) Mairs burger vnd Mayster des böckhenhandtwerchs alhie', orders 'der dorffmaister zu Rumb(?) Thoman Egger' to announce to a man 'daselbs meiner richterlichen Jurisdiction sizendt', whose name is read 'Vinckl(?)', 'ainen ordenlich Schäzrechtstag' on 17 November 'aldort zue Rumb(?) in ... Vinckls(?) Wirts behausung' over 200 fl. capital; 'Datum Hall den 1. Novembris 16[5]4'. Thoman Egger is thus more probably the village officer who serves the notice than the debtor; the place name, written the same way in the second form on 230-1r ('zu Rumb(?), mein[er Pf]legsverwaltung'), is read Rumb or Stumb by the research reader (possibly Rum near Hall) and 'Stamm[.]' (Stams?) by a blind reader whose context showed the word Stams, so the place is not settled, and the third digit of the year is uncertain (1634 or 1644 not excluded). Item 230-1r has two blank forms of a Pfleger's order to pay 250 fl. within 14 days ('Forma aines 14 tägigen Verschaffts'), 230-3 is a slip with a few cut-off words, and the other faces are blank. No printed formulary with these forms was found by full-text search in the Munich digital library and Google Books; the Tyrolean Landesordnung of 1573, read on the page at Book 2 tit. XXXV and LXVI, prescribes the summons 'zu hauß vnd zu hof oder vnder augen' and the valuation of pledges but prints no forms, and no outside record of the case was found. No human review.

content.title: Model notice of a valuation court day ('Schäz(?) Fürpottzet[l]')
content.description: The Stadtrichter of Hall ('N.'), at the suit of Kilgen(?) Mair, burgher and master baker of Hall, orders notice of a Schäzrechtstag on 17 November over 200 fl. capital, to be held at Rumb(?) in the house of an innkeeper read Vinckl(?); Thoman Egger is named, more probably as the Dorfmeister who serves the notice than as the debtor. Dated Hall, 1 November 16[5]4.
content.remarks: The judge is written 'N.', so this is a model or copy. The place is not settled (Rum near Hall or Stams). The third digit of the year is uncertain.

content.title: Forma aines 14 tägigen Verschaffts
content.description: Two blank model forms for an order of a Pfleger to pay a debt within 14 days; the second names the same place as the notice (Rumb(?)).

identification: Two German documents: (1) piece 3v, undated draft letter of the abbot and convent of Stams to a prince whose father was 'Hertzog Fridrich' (inferred to be Duke, later Archduke, Sigmund of Tyrol), asking that Fridrich's foundation of a perpetual sung Mass with lights in the abbey, endowed with 100 ducats at Lueg(?) and 100 at the office in Hall, be kept up; the foundation corresponds to Duke Friedrich IV's charter of 12 April 1409 (Stams StiA Urk. A XCIII 4); (2) pieces 1-2v, fragments of a separate private letter about a dead sister and an inheritance, mentioning Stams
note: Piece 3v, a corrected draft without seal or date, names its sender only as 'Abbt und der gantz convent zu Sta[ms]' (no abbot's name is written) and its addressee only as a prince whose father was 'Hertzog Fridrich'; 'Lueg', '[ampt]hauss' and 'Sta[ms]' rest partly on the modern typescript mounted with the piece. The two 100-ducat revenues match Friedrich IV's Stiftbrief of 12 April 1409 (regest opened on monasterium.net), and in the next charter of the same group, A XCIII 5 of 11 November 1482 (read on its image), Archduke Sigmund recalls the same grant by 'Hertzog Fridreich ... vnnser lieber herr vnd vater', notes that Stams had been given only four pounds Berner per ducat, and orders payment at the current rate. That supports the inference that the addressee is Sigmund; it mentions no petition, and the cause of the 'merklicher abgang' the draft complains of is unread, so whether the draft relates to that order is not established, and its date stays within 1446-1490. The typed figures added on the typescript read '28./12 1408' and '1409 12/4' (the second the date of the foundation charter) and do not date the letter; pieces 1-2 are a separate private letter without names or date; no human review.

fragmentarium.title: Draft letter of Stams Abbey; fragments of a private letter

content.title: Draft letter of the abbot and convent of Stams to a prince, probably Duke Sigmund of Tyrol
content.description: The abbot and convent ask the prince, whose father Duke Friedrich founded a perpetual sung Mass with lights in the abbey, endowed with 100 ducats at Lueg (?) and 100 at the office in Hall, that the foundation be kept up. Undated; no abbot named.
content.remarks: The foundation corresponds to Duke Friedrich IV's charter of 12 April 1409 (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Urk. A XCIII 4). An order of Archduke Sigmund of 11 November 1482 (Urk. A XCIII 5) recalls the same grant by his father and directs that the ducats be paid at their current value; it does not mention this letter.

content.title: Private letter
content.description: Fragments of a letter about a dead sister and an inheritance, mentioning Stams. Writer, addressee and date lost.

identification: Latin excerpt notes agreeing with, and probably taken from, Chrysostomus Henriquez, Fasciculus Sanctorum Ordinis Cisterciensis (Brussels 1623; Cologne 1631): the tally of St Bernard's miracles on his German journey (1631 ed. p. 100) and the Life of St Robert of Newminster (lib. I, dist. 11; 1631 ed. pp. 251-253); with a partly read German protocol before Abbot Thoma[n/s] of Stams on the other face
note: On piece 174-2r a list headed 'S. Bern. in peregrinatioe germania fecit miracula' (Ceci 173, Claudi 158, Contracti 15, Muti 53, Surdi 65, Paralytici 11, Manus aridae 55, 'Aliaque innumerabilia') agrees in order and every number with Henriquez's summary, checked on page images of the 1631 and 1623 editions; no earlier printed tally was found, a negative search. The following notes on St Robert (abstinence; all monks predestined 'praeter duos Conversos'; 'alligat[us]'; a figure 'in forma rustici' in the choir; 'falso accusatur'; death with Editha) follow Henriquez's Life of Robert of Newminster in sequence and key words, not continuous wording. The life was printed earlier by Capgrave (1516) and Surius (1572), but the notes reproduce Henriquez's margin headings 'Omnes Monachi eius sunt praedestinati' and 'Falso accusatur', absent from Surius 1572, so Henriquez is the probable source (the headings are short, and an intermediary cannot be ruled out) and the notes probably date from 1623 or later; a second research reader made this comparison on page images, Capgrave only in the 1901 edition text. The devotional tags at the head of the panel are unidentified. The German entry on 174-1v ('Actum den [?]29 Tag Monatt Mart[ij]? / Vor ... Herrn Thoma[n/s] Abbt zu St[...]', about a reckoning and interest at Untermieming and nearby places) is only partly read and its year is not legible; the pencil date '1621 Aug. 29' is wrong on the month. No human review.

identification: Leaf of a German handwritten newsletter (writer, place and date lost; script 16th century): five men, probably described as spreading 'Ketzerey und Sectt', seized by peasants in a barn, questioned publicly on a Friday about their 'lere und glaub' and strangled; daily burnings, beheadings and tongue-cuttings; on the other face the wonders of a man titled 'profet', 'propst' or 'profos' (word not settled), who made the dumb speak, healed the lame and blind and raised the dead
note: Both faces were reread on the image. One face reports that 'Vergangnen Monntags diß monats' peasants in a village (name struck out, replacement above the line unread) seized five men who had come there, probably 'in willens ir Ketzerey und Sectt daselbs weytter zubraitten', 'in ainem Stadl'; they were handed to the authorities, questioned before a crowd 'freytags hernach' about their 'lere und glaub', would not speak or confess, and 'dieselben fünff lebendig stranguliert, oder erstöckht worden'; a further paragraph begins 'Es ist schier khain tag da man nit etliche ... prenndt, köpfft ... zungen abschneidt'. The other face says that when 'gedachter pro[..]t' came he made a young man 'ganntz stumb und redloß' since birth speak, that the dead crept alive out of their graves, ate and drank, and 'Er macht die lamen, stumen, gehörlosen, gerad, gesundt, die plinden gesehendt'; the noun was read 'propst' in the first reading and by a blind reader (low confidence), but 'profet' and 'profos' also fit the letters, and the sense of the whole face depends on it. The leaf has no date, and the pencil note 'aus IX/66 v. J. 1641-' is modern and concerns only the host volume. Full-text searches in MDZ, Google Books and the Internet Archive found no printed counterpart; Quellen zur Geschichte der Täufer (Österreich) and VD16 were not checked.

content.title: Newsletter (writer, place and date lost)
content.description: One face: five men, probably described as spreading 'Ketzerey und Sectt', seized by peasants in a barn on a Monday, questioned publicly on the Friday after about their 'lere und glaub' and strangled; daily burnings, beheadings and tongue-cuttings of others. Other face: the wonders of a man titled 'profet', 'propst' or 'profos' (word not settled), who made the dumb speak, healed the lame and the blind and raised the dead.
content.remarks: The place, the writer and the addressee are not named; the village name is struck out and its replacement is unread.

identification: Single-voice part-book leaves of polyphonic church music, composer and works unidentified: one voice of a Mass Ordinary (Kyrie to Osanna); one voice of a Marian piece on a Latin text that is probably verse in elegiac couplets ('nos ergo miseros Sancta Maria ui[..] / vulnera nostra le-ua'); a part headed 'A 8. Secundo' with the text cue 'Lucis inaccess: Vi[..]', probably 'Lucis inaccess[ae] Vi[rgo]'; and a florid part in another hand cued '[..]n wir im Leben sind'
note: Eight paper pieces of mensural music from bindings: 15-4r/v and 15-5v carry one voice of a Mass (Kyrie, Gloria, Credo to 'et homo factus est', 'Dominus Deus Sa[baoth]', 'Osanna in excelsis', F clef on 15-4r), 15-2v one voice of a Marian piece, 15-7r a part headed 'A 8. Secundo' with the cue 'Lucis inaccess: Vi[..]', probably 'Lucis inaccess[ae] Vi[rgo]', and 15-1r, in another hand with lozenge note heads, the German cue '[..]n wir im Leben sind' (opening line of 'Mitten wir im Leben sind'). The words on 15-2v ('[..]gia se solium fecit habere [..]am', '[..]or plus pollet et audet', 'efflagitata venit', 'nos ergo miseros Sancta Maria ui[..] / vulnera nostra le ua') are probably verse in elegiac couplets, since 'plus pollet et audet' closes like a hexameter and 'vulnera nostra le-ua' like a pentameter; the text's source and liturgical use are not established. Neither Latin text was found by phrase search in Google Books, the Internet Archive, the Munich digital library or Corpus Corporum, nor by text search in RISM, including the records of the Stams music archive, and a RISM incipit search on the Kyrie opening as tentatively read gave no relevant hit. No composer, title or owner's note survives; modern pencil notes ('aus Urbar IV/42 vom J. 1625', 'Einband v. II/16 ... aus dem Jahre 155[.]') name the host bindings and date those, not the music.

identification: Figural church music, composer unidentified (Magnificat; a piece with the psalm verse 'Confitebor tibi in populis Domine'; Kyrie), with German devotional prose written over one leaf; a printed German almanac page (November, 1644-1699) adhering face down to 16-6v carries the description of Strasbourg from Martin Zeiller / Matthaeus Merian, Topographia Alsatiae, 'Straßburg' (1663 ed., pp. 51-52)
note: Seven paper pieces of music in score and in parts, of the 17th or 18th century by estimate from the notation: a Magnificat ('quia fecit', 'qui potens: et sanctum nomen ej[us]', 'Fecit potentiam'), a piece with the words 'Confitebor tibi in populis Domine' entered in mid-page on 16-2v (a verse of Psalms 56 and 107, so not necessarily its opening words), and a Kyrie in full score; no composer, title or date is written, and on the two faces reread (16-2v, 16-7r) the staff lines are too worn for a secure melodic incipit. RISM has no record with this psalm verse among the holdings of the Stams music archive, and an incipit search on the Kyrie bass entry as tentatively read gave no relevant hit, so no setting is named. Over the music on 16-1r are about twenty lines of German prose in Kurrent on the barren tree cast into eternal fire, read in part and not found in print. A thin printed paper layer stuck face down to 16-6v, read mirrored, is one almanac page with November day rows, an old-style/new-style day table ten days apart and a prose column, two passages of which agree in wording with Merian's Topographia Alsatiae of 1663 on page images (the 1644 edition by OCR only); this places the almanac page in 1644-1699 and dates neither the music nor the prose, and the almanac's title, year and printer are not identified.

identification: Revers of Cristoff Camerlannder(?) 'auf dem Prenner' for the hereditary tenancy of the whole Oberwißhof on the Brenner (the later Brennerbad), a holding of the 'Gotshaus Stambs', bought with the consent of Abbot Johann as ground lord; dated in November, year lost ('Fünffzehenhundert[...]'; no decade read), by inference from outside records between 1565 and 1569; one paper sheet in two pieces, text mirror-reversed; plus a printed Latin scrap with the Liber pontificalis life of Sixtus II, edition not identified
note: The mirror-reversed German text on both pieces is one document, read from a flipped image with the outside records in view: piece 11_2 holds the middle and 11_1 the end of each line, with about ten letters also lost at the junction, and the left third of the sheet, with the start of every line and the year, is lost. 'Cristoff Camerlannder' ('[...]lannder auf dem Prenner, im Lanndtger[icht]'; a blind reader read the name 'Cristoff H[..]n[.]lst[..]nder', so the surname is not confirmed on the leaf alone) promises to keep his 'erkhaufften gannzen Oberwißhof' (a blind reader: 'Obermaiß hoff') in repair and not to alienate it without the consent of the abbot ('Johannsen Abbte, vnd Regierenden Prelaten') and to pay his dues to the 'Gotshaus Stambs'; the farm is described with 'ain grosser, vnd ain Clainer Rosstal', a bake-oven, fields and gardens 'alles bey vn[d anainan]der gelegen, allain geet die gemain Lanndtstrassen mitten', the 'Wechsel hof' and 'Khofl' as neighbours and 'Vier Rechts Perckhmäder sambt ainer Khäser', and the dating clause reads '[...] Monats Nouembris Nach der gepurt Jhesu Cr[isti] ... Fünffzehenhundert[...]'. The Stams Revers of Thoman Vogl of 11 December 1569 (K LXII 3, image read) names Cristoff Camerlannder 'auf dem Prenner, Lanndtgerichts Sterzingen gesessen' as seller of the same Oberwißhof and repeats the description almost word for word (it adds the inn, wild bath and mill, which fall in the fragment's lost parts), and Auckenthaler's farm history (1953, pp. 66-67, snippets) has Christoph Kamerlander as bath-keeper there in 1565; the Stams regests name Abbot Georg in September 1565 and Abbot Johannes from October 1567, so the act falls, by inference, between 1565 and 1569 (no decade is read on the leaf). The act itself was not found among the 25 Stams regests of November 1565 to December 1569 on monasterium.net (a list that also lacks the 1560 Tschugg Revers for the same farm, so it is incomplete), the seller (read 'Niclas(?) Tschugg(?)') is not established, and the printed Liber pontificalis strip remains without an identified edition; no human review.

fragmentarium.title: Revers of Cristoff Camerlannder (?) for the Oberwißhof on the Brenner (Stams Abbey); printed Liber pontificalis

content.title: Revers of Cristoff Camerlannder (?) for the Oberwißhof on the Brenner
content.persons: Cristoff Camerlannder; Johann, Abbot of Stams
content.description: One sheet in two pieces (11_2 middle, 11_1 right; left third lost). Cristoff Camerlannder 'auf dem Prenner' acknowledges holding the whole Oberwißhof (house, stables, bake-oven, four mountain meadows) of the 'Gotshaus Stambs' by hereditary tenancy, with the consent of Abbot Johann, and binds himself to the usual tenant's obligations. Dated in November; year lost, between 1565 and 1569, probably 1567, 1568 or 1569.
content.remarks: Mirror-reversed. The Stams Revers of Thoman Vogl, 11 December 1569 (K LXII 3), names Camerlannder as seller of the same farm and describes it in the same words, adding the inn, wild bath and mill. No outside record of this act was found.

content.remarks: The edition is not identified.

identification: Vertical strip cut from the middle of a German parchment sale deed (Kaufbrief), probably 16th century: a sale involving a [P/B]aumbgarten and a sum in gulden, with warranty and Gewährschaft clauses; issuer, buyer, property, place and year lost
note: About 30 lines of German chancery cursive were read on the image of the recto, each cut at both ends so that only 3 to 5 words of a line survive. The sale is shown by 'Vnd verkhaufft' (twice), 'alle Khauff[...]', the warranty 'Rechtenmacht vnd gwalt' and '[ge]werscha[fft]'; the strip also names '[P/B]aumbgarten', 'ain gulden Rannsch..' (possibly 'Ra?nisch', Rhenish, not 'vngerisch'), a 'Durchleüchtigkhait' and, in the display line, 'des Edlen Hochgelerten ?['. Two fresh readers given neutral crops confirmed the display line, the verb and 'Durchleüchtigkhait'; the adjudication left the initial of the orchard word unverified and the year word undecided as 'Vi?z[en/ig](?)' after '...hündert, vnnd', so neither ...14 nor ...40 can be read and the year is not converted. The 16th-century date rests on script and spelling only; a modern blue label on the back, 'Urbari W?ss?brun(n)(?) 1593', probably names the host volume and is not used as evidence for the deed. No party, place or year survives to search with; sibling Stams strips Frg. 54, 55, 57, 59, 211 and 224 were compared without a join, and monasterium.net was not checked. The result stops at partial because only the genre and the action are established; no human review.

content.title: Deed of sale (Kaufbrief)
content.description: Middle strip of a deed of sale with warranty and Gewährschaft clauses, naming a [P/B]aumbgarten and a sum in gulden. Issuer, buyer, property, place and year are lost.

identification: Last leaf of a Latin account of receipts (Receptae) of a religious house, probably Stams abbey (inferred, not named), fifteenth century, probably its last third, with 23 receipt items and the grand total of 1,549 marks; accountant and year not on the leaf
note: Both faces were read on the image: 23 entries for sales of silver, salt 'in Glurns et in alys locis', herrings, hemp, four oxen 'ad curiam principis', cows, mares, wine and cloth, money 'in resignatione officiorum fratris Johannis Trientt[..](?)', receipts from an infirmarian and a prebendary and 'de Sal[in/m]a et theolono ad pistrinum', closing with 'Suma omnium Receptarum prescriptarum marce Mille Quingente quadraginta nouem lb vna gr xj(?) q iiij'. The buyers are 'Johanne Metzger de Vmbst(?)' (Vmbst is a spelling of Imst attested in Zingerle's medieval Tyrolean inventories; the letters still need an independent reading), 'Oswaldo kopp de Talfs' and 'Cunrado Nägelin de Siltz(?)'; Stams charter regests on monasterium.net have a Hanns Mezger with land at Imst in 1474 (B_XVIII_2, B_XVIII_3) and a Konrad Nägele selling to the abbey in 1480 (B_XVIII_9, L_XXIII_15), which show such men dealing with Stams then, not this account. Stams is therefore probable but not named, and the year is not fixed: the only date is a modern pencil '(c.14[.]1', and Rhenish florins are reckoned at 5 lb. Searches inside the Album Stamsense and Lebersorg's chronicle did not find the friar, and the abbey's account series was not consulted.

content.title: Account of receipts (Receptae) of a religious house, probably Stams
content.description: Last leaf, with 23 receipt items: silver, salt sold in Glurns and elsewhere, herrings, hemp, oxen sold to the prince's court, cattle, wine and cloth sold to people 'de Vmbst(?)' (Imst?), 'de Talfs' (Telfs) and 'de Siltz(?)' (Silz?), money on the resignation of the offices of brother Johannes Trientt[..] (?), receipts from an infirmarian and a prebendary, and 'de Sal[in/m]a et theolono ad pistrinum'. Total: Suma omnium Receptarum prescriptarum marce Mille Quingente quadraginta nouem.
content.remarks: Accountant and year not on the leaf. Stams is probable from the holding, the monastic offices and the Upper Inn valley places, but is not named. A Hanns Mezger with land at Imst (1474) and a Konrad Nägele (1480) occur in the Stams charters (monasterium.net, AT-StiAStams, B_XVIII_2, B_XVIII_9); whether they are the buyers named here is not shown. Rhenish florins are reckoned at 5 lb.

identification: 21 paper pieces from the binding of Stams Hs 25: (6-1r) undated German draft letter of an unnamed religious house (probably Stams, inferred) to an unnamed mediator, asking him not to take up Baltasar Hustadl/Heustadel, to whom Duke Sigmund had granted a free safe-conduct, and to help make peace for the house, c. 1446-1490; (6-2 to 6-21) Latin wage and settlement notes for servants, with dated entries in the 1440s (read xliij and xliiij) and a reference back to 'anno xlij'
note: The letter on 6-1r names 'hertzogh sigmund', 'dem baltasar hustadl ain freyes gelait', the addressee as 'gůter gůnner vn(d) mittler baiden tailen', noblemen 'in schwabe land' and 'vnserm gotzhaws', but neither sender nor addressee, and has no date; the range c. 1446-1490 rests on Sigmund's ducal style and outside mentions of Heustadl. The sender is probably Stams: Lebersorg's Stams chronicle (ed. Haidacher 2000, no preview) has Heustadl on a page where Fehde, Schaden and Entschädigung also occur (p. 339) and on a page where 1453, 1454, Krieg, Sigmund, Freiberg and Eisenberg also occur (p. 283), but these are word probes of pages that could not be read, not a record of this letter. A Konstanz regest (Villingen, 7 August 1469) has Duke Sigmund asking the town to release the arrested Walthasar Hewstadel, and his 1478 Urfehde is in Chmel and Regesta Imperii; no record of the letter was found by searches of monasterium.net (Stams fonds) and the RI open data. The wage notes have dated entries 'anno domini etc xl..' in the forties (no hundreds written), read xliij and xliiij by the research reader and a checker (a blind reader confirmed 'anno d(omi)ni ... xl' but not the units), a reference back to 'de anno xlij', and an isolated 'xlvj' (6-7r) that may be a year or a sum; and name a servant 'de Silz' on 6-14r and Johannes Straigl on 6-12r; the pencil '1463' on 6-3r is a modern note, and about half the account faces were looked at without transcription.

content.title: Draft letter concerning Baltasar Hustadl
content.persons: Sigmund, duke of Austria; Baltasar Hustadl
content.description: A religious house, probably Stams, asks an unnamed mediator not to take up Baltasar Hustadl (Heustadel), to whom Duke Sigmund had granted a free safe-conduct, and to help make peace for the house. Sender and addressee are not named; undated, c. 1446-1490.
content.remarks: A Balthasar Heustadel of Imst is attested 1454-1478; in 1469 Duke Sigmund asked Konstanz to release a Walthasar Hewstadel, probably the same man (regest by snippet).

content.title: Wage and settlement notes for servants
content.description: Dated entries in the 1440s (read xliij and xliiij), a reference back to 'anno xlij', and an isolated 'xlvj' that may be a year or a sum; one servant is 'de Silz'.

identification: Lengthwise strip from a German deed: a first-person issuer, for himself and his heirs, conveys a meadow ('mannmadt wisen') with bounds and appurtenances for a sum in Mark Berner acknowledged as paid; place possibly 'Stambs(?)'; dated in a 19th year ('[..]euntzechenden'), century not on the image; parties lost
note: A strip 55 mm wide from the middle of a German parchment deed keeps 3-5 words of each of 32 lines, read on the image: 'mein erben das ich', 'wissentlich', bounds ('[..]d strass. Gegen mitt[ag]', 'den genanten Stra[ss]'), 'mannmadt wisen', 'vnuerband(?)', '[da]r zu gehort', '[m]arckh zal perner', 'vnnd bezalt sein', 'nach dato ditz brie[fs]', a names line '[..]l pondl(?) [..]tassar b[..]', '[..]effen am Stambs(?)' and the year word '[..]euntzechenden'. The word check confirmed '[..]euntzechenden' letter by letter (n and t before the z exclude '[vi]erzehenden'), 'marckh zal perner' and 'Stambs(?)' with its query; 'pondl(?)' stays uncertain and 'Bal-' of '[Bal]tassar' is supplied, not read. The year word gives a 19th year, but the century is not on the image; the hand suggests the sixteenth century, which is not evidence of the year. The clauses point to a sale of a meadow with a quittance for the price, but issuer, buyer, place and the price itself are lost at both cut edges, so the result stops at the genre. A note 'Malser Urbarium I/38' on the back, a later addition hidden by the catalogue mask, suggests the strip came from the binding of an urbar for Mals; this is a lead to the host volume, untested. No outside search was possible without names; no human review.

content.title: Conveyance of a meadow (?)
content.description: A first-person issuer, for himself and his heirs, conveys a meadow ('mannmadt wisen') with its bounds and appurtenances for a sum in Mark Berner acknowledged as paid. Dated in a 19th year ('[..]euntzechenden'); the century is not given. Parties and price are lost.
content.remarks: Place possibly 'Stambs(?)'. A note 'Malser Urbarium I/38' on the back suggests the strip came from the binding of an urbar of Mals.

identification: Renunciation (Verzichtbrief) of 154[.]: married couples (names lost) renounce all hereditary claims to the goods of the late Herr Cristoff T[...], possibly parish priest of Untermieming ('zu Vnder[m]iemingen(?)', enhanced image), which an abbot and convent, probably of Stams (on the setting: the Petersberg seal, the Silz witnesses, the Stams Urbar cover), had taken into their hands; sealed by Veit Ca[ss/st]le (possibly the Veit Castl of 1564), Pfleger and Kastner of St. Petersberg; day 'am Ersten', month and unit of the year lost
note: The document is on the inner face of the cover of the Stams Oberkellneramt Urbar for 1594 (Hs. 140), read rotated 180 degrees; the opening lines with the issuers are abraded beyond reading and the last line is cut through. Read in colour are the renunciation clauses, 'wir obbenanndte Wirtleüt', the sealer 'Veitten Ca[ss/st]le diezeit Phleger vnd Castner zu Sannt Pettersperg', 'Herr L[e/o]uin(?) Cordier(?) diezeit Pharrer zu Sylz', Hanns Jörg Sturm, Sebastian Welsch and Petter Stöckhl of Silz, 'Beschehen am Ersten' and '[...]vnd vierzigisten Jar'. Read on a contrast-enhanced image are 'Herrn Abbt vnd prelaten zu Stams' and 'verstorbne Pharrers(?) zu Vnder[m]iemingen Herrn Cristoffen T[.]nnckh[..]mers(?)'; a blind reader confirmed 'herren Abbt vnd prelaten(?)' and 'verstorb-' but read 'für(?) Ma[...]' where 'zu Stams' is claimed and gave only '-mmingen(?)' without 'Pharr-'. So the house is probably Stams on the setting (seal, witnesses, the Stams Urbar cover) and the deceased possibly the parish priest of Untermieming, a parish under Stams patronage. A Veit Castl is Pfleger and Kastner of St. Petersberg on 17 April 1564 (Munich, BayHStA, Kloster Frauenchiemsee Urk. 1208), showing the man and office in that year only; no record of this act was found in the Stams charter regests on monasterium.net, and the issuers are lost, so the result stays partial.

content.title: Renunciation (Verzichtbrief)
content.persons: Cristoff T[...]; Veit Ca[ss/st]le; Hanns Jörg Sturm; Sebastian Welsch; Petter Stöckhl
content.description: Married couples (names lost) renounce for themselves and their heirs all hereditary claims to the goods of the late Herr Cristoff T[...], probably parish priest of Untermieming, which an abbot and convent, probably of Stams, had taken into their hands. Sealed by Veit Ca[ss/st]le (probably Veit Castl), Pfleger and Kastner of St. Petersberg; the parish priest of Silz and three residents of Silz are named. 154[.], 'am Ersten' of a lost month.
content.remarks: 'zu Stams' and 'zu Vnder[m]iemingen' are read on a contrast-enhanced image of the abraded upper lines and have not been independently checked.

identification: Thirty-seven spine-lining strips from two Latin documents: (I) a curial or judicial act on an appeal involving the syndics and community of an unnamed place, a bishop and a judge 'Ber[..]um', with a date recited in the text ('[mille]simo qu-' under a Pope 'Joha[..]', so John XXIII, probably May 1411) and, probably of the same document, an eschatocol of a Saturday in January, pontifical year 2 (23 or 30 January 1412 if the two belong together); (II) a land contract with numbered conditions and a boundary clause; parties and place not read
note: On 87-3r the dating row reads '[..]simo qu[..] ... Indictio[..] quarta(?) ... dicti Joha[..] p(a)p(e)(?) vigesi[..](?) [..]i tercy(?) [..]e quar[..] mens[..] [.]ay', and the body has 'appell(aci)on(em) huiusmodi', 'sindicos', 'et vniu(er)si[..]atem', 'romana curia' and 'p(re)fatum d(omi)n(u)m Ber[..]um Jud[..]'; 87-2r has 'die Saba[..] [..]igesim[..] mens[..] Januar[..] qui[..](?) Ind[..]ionis ... Sanctissimi d(omi)ni ... p(re)fat[..] ... secundo', which fits January 1412 under John XXIII if 87-2r belongs with 87-3r; standing alone its year is open. The words 'quarta', 'vigesimi tercii' and 'quinte' were read with a modern red note on the carrier in view ('1411, Ind 4 ... Johannes pp XXIII', '1412, Samstag, 23. Januar') and were not confirmed by a blind reader, so the indiction argument is dropped; '[mille]simo qu-' with 'Joha[..]' in the pope's place (read also by a blind reader) already points to John XXIII. The 87-3r row is a date recited inside the text (a terminus post quem), not the document's date; that 87-3r and 87-2r are one document is probable, not shown. 87-1r, in another hand, is a land contract with 'Tercio', 'pena', 'obnoxy', 'ab alio late[..]', 'vocabu[..]', 'Anthony' and the name-like words 'valpelin[.]' and 'val solo'. Modern pencil and red crayon mark all three groups as taken from 'Hs. 56'; the Stams charters of 1411-1414 on monasterium.net have no counterpart, and no party or place is read.

content.title: Curial or judicial act on an appeal
content.description: An appeal involving the syndics and community of an unnamed place, a bishop, a judge Ber[..] and the Roman curia. The dating row of 87-3r is read as indiction 'quarta(?)' and a Pope John 'vigesi[..](?) ... tercy(?)' (1411 if so); 87-2r is dated on a Saturday in January, 'qui[..](?) Indictionis', in the second year of a pope, probably 23 or 30 January 1412.
content.remarks: That 87-3r and 87-2r are one document is probable, not established; taken alone, 87-2r also fits January 1442 or 1457. The pope's name and the indictions were read with the modern red note on the carrier in view. Parties and place not read. Modern pencil on the carrier ('aus Hs. 56') and red crayon on the reverses ('Hs 56') name the host volume of all three groups.

content.title: Land contract
content.description: With numbered conditions, a penalty clause and a boundary clause; parties, place and year not read.

identification: Liturgical calendar of the use of Auxerre: a name column for 17-23 July (Theodosius ep., Arnulf ep., Arsenius conf., Marinus conf., Praxedis, Mary Magdalene, Apollinaris) and two strips of golden numbers and Sunday letters (probably mid-August) with 'festum duplex'
note: Three strips of a graded liturgical calendar. The name strip has Theodosius bishop, Arnulf bishop, Arsenius confessor, Marinus confessor, Praxedis, Mary Magdalene and Apollinaris for 17-23 July, the same seven feasts on the same days as the calendar of the Auxerre missal Paris, BnF, Latin 17312 and the printed Auxerre missal dated 1487 (the 1532 Auxerre missal agrees except for 'Martini' on 20 July), compared on page images; the printed calendars of Troyes, Nevers, Autun, Paris and Orléans lack Theodosius on 17 July and Marinus on 20 July. The other two strips have golden numbers, Sunday letters and 'festum duplex' without names, probably for mid-August (23-25 March is not excluded). Calendars of Sens, Langres, Chartres and the religious orders were not compared; the church within the diocese and the date are not established.

fragmentarium.title: Calendar
fragmentarium.subtitle: Use of Auxerre

content.title: Calendar, use of Auxerre, July and August
content.description: Names for 17-23 July (Theodosius ep., Arnulf ep., Arsenius conf., Marinus conf., Praxedis, Mary Magdalene, Apollinaris); golden numbers and Sunday letters, probably for mid-August, with 'festum duplex'.
content.remarks: The seven July feasts stand on the same days in the calendar of the Auxerre missal Paris, BnF, Latin 17312 and in the printed Auxerre missals of 1487 and 1532; Theodosius and Marinus are absent from the printed calendars of Troyes, Nevers, Autun, Paris and Orléans. The church within the diocese and the date are not established.

bibliography: Paris, BnF, Latin 17312, calendar (July)
Missale Autissiodorense (Paris: Jean Du Pré, 1487?), calendar (July)

identification: Piece 30.14, darker cursive column: Peregrinus de Opole, Sermones de sanctis, sermon for All Souls 'Gaudete cum gaudentibus ... Duo festa pariter agit ecclesia' (Schneyer IV, Peregrinus de Opole S80). Pieces 30.12r and 30.8r (faded rubricated book hand): three sermons that also stand in the anonymous Sermones de sanctis of Kiel, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. ms. Bord. 92 - the end of the sermon for Philip and James followed directly, as in Kiel, by 'Exaltasti super terram' for the Invention of the Cross, and 'Ascendit deus in iubilacione' for the Ascension, which has a different rubric and a different text before it. The other pieces are unidentified
note: The darker cursive column of 30.14 agrees in wording and sequence with Peregrinus's All Souls sermon in the 1501 Sermones (BSB bsb00011329, scans 305-306), with variants such as 'et mortuorum' and 'quamdiu pulsantur et sepeliuntur'. On the faded textualis, 30.12r has '[unus] ex phariseis ... arripuit ... in caput ... tali mart[irio] ... sepultus ib[idem]', a rubric for the Invention of the Cross and '[Ex]altasti super terram ... verba ... gratias agens ... [appe]llans lignum', and 30.8r has under the rubric 'In ascensione domini' '[As]cendit deus in iubil... celebramus ... super omnes celos id est super omnes angelos videntibus apostolis et beata Maria ... volens relinquere ... peregrinatus fuit xxxiii ... patriam celestem'; both agree with an anonymous collection of Sermones de sanctis read on page images of Kiel, Cod. ms. Bord. 92 (fols. 7ra and 15vb), with small differences ('id est' for 'et', 'apostolis' for 'discipulis'). The Invention of the Cross rubric and the incipit 'Exaltasti super terram' were read only with the Kiel text in view (a blind reader did not confirm them), while the James passage and the Ascension opening were also read by a blind reader. The text before the Ascension rubric is not that of the Kiel manuscript at the same point, and the rubric is 'In ascensione domini' where Kiel has 'Sermo secundus', so the fragment's book did not have the Kiel arrangement there; and a St George rubric reported on 30.9v was not reread. The cursive piece 30.2, the diagram piece 30.4 and the remaining pieces are unplaced, so the record stays partial; no human review.

fragmentarium.title: Sermons

content.title: Peregrinus de Opole, Sermones de sanctis, sermon for All Souls, Gaudete cum gaudentibus et flete cum flentibus (Rom 12:15)
content.description: Opening of the sermon (30.14v) and a passage about 35 printed lines later (30.14r). Inc.: Gaudete cum gaudentibus flete cum flentibus Ad romanos xij ... Duo festa pariter sancta ecclesia agit.
content.remarks: Whether this column belongs to the same book as the columns beside it is not established.

content.title: Sermones de sanctis: Philip and James, Invention of the Cross, Ascension (three sermons that also stand in Kiel, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. ms. Bord. 92)
content.description: 30.12r: end of the sermon for Philip and James (expl. sepultus ib[idem]), rubric for the Invention of the Cross, inc. [Ex]altasti super terram. 30.8r: rubric In ascensione domini, inc. [As]cendit deus in iubil... Hodie celebramus [diem] quo ... ascendit super omnes celos id est super omnes angelos.
content.remarks: Compared with Kiel, Cod. ms. Bord. 92, fols. 7ra and 15vb; the Ascension sermon has a different rubric and a different text before it in the fragment. Other pieces in the same hand, including one with a rubric for St George, were not compared.

content.title: Unidentified pieces
content.remarks: The other pieces, including a piece in a dense cursive hand (30.2) and a piece with a diagram (30.4), are not identified.

bibliography: J. B. Schneyer, Repertorium der lateinischen Sermones des Mittelalters, IV, Peregrinus de Opole, no. 80
Peregrinus de Opole, Sermones (1501)
Kiel, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. ms. Bord. 92, fols. 7r, 15v (description by K. Schnabel, Handschriftenportal)

F. Lackner, Katalog der mittelalterlichen Handschriften bis zum Ende des 16. Jahrhunderts in der Zentralbibliothek der Wiener Franziskanerprovinz in Graz (Vienna 2006), Cod. A 67/29 (not seen; cited from the Kiel description)

identification: Left part of a German enfeoffment deed, first half of the 16th century(?): grantors who call themselves 'vnnser der Verleiher' grant fields, meadows and tithes at Mals and Burg[ei]s in the upper Vinschgau to Crysten(?) P[..]ü[..](?) as Lehentrager, at a rent of 'Sechsunddre[issig]' due at St Martin and St Gallus(?); grantor and year lost; reused as the wrapper of a 1550 'Diener und Ehalten Geding'
note: The left third or less of the lines was read on the image of the recto: plots 'zu Mall[s]' and 'zu Burgeus(?)' bounded by the common road and the common Waal, the words 'an vnnser der Verleiher vnnd des Go[tshaus]' and '[ge]dachts Gotshaus Sannt Maria perg [...] pawt', a grant to 'Crysten(?) P[..]ü[..](?) als Lehentrager' (Cristan or Cryspin- also possible), a ban on partition, sale only 'nach Lanndsrecht', a rent 'Namblich Sechsunddre[issig]' due 'auff Sannt Martins' and 'auf ainen Jeden Sannd Galle[n]'(?), and a last line read by a blind reader as 'thuen . auch den Lanndsrechten ... vnnd yetzgemachter gepundte', not the opening of a dating clause; the year is lost. The grantor is not read: Marienberg, named with 'gedachts' and so mentioned earlier, Stams, which had land and tithe at Mals and Burgeis, renewed its tenancies around Mals in 1539-1547 and keeps the strip, and a lay lord are all possible. The neighbours read as 'Melchior [.]attutsch(?)' (a blind reader: 'Melchior Ha[....]tzch'), 'Claus [G/B]ro[...]' and 'Clagut(?) Pruggls Erben' are possibly Burgeis people of the Marienberg charters on monasterium.net (a Melchior Matutsch zu Burgeis, 24 March 1545, Urkunden VI/385; the Prügl family; the forename Clagut), and the Lehentrager is possibly a Christian Pritzi of Burgeis (named 1549); this is consistent with the first half of the 16th century but does not narrow it, and these names, the underlined word in line 6 (a personal name(?) rather than 'Stifftung') and the last line still need an independent reading. No record of the act was found by searching the Stams and Marienberg fonds on monasterium.net; the reuse label 'Der diener und Ehalten Gedinng 1550' gives a terminus only if written at reuse; no human review.

content.title: Enfeoffment of fields, meadows and tithes at Mals and Burgeis
content.description: Left part of the deed. Grantors who call themselves 'Verleiher' grant fields, meadows and tithes at Mals and Burg[ei]s to Crysten(?) P[..]ü[..](?) as Lehenträger, at a rent of 'Sechsunddre[issig]' due at St Martin and St Gallus(?). Grantor and year are lost.
content.remarks: The text names 'gedachts Gotshaus Sannt Maria perg' (Marienberg) and neighbours read as Melchior [.]attutsch(?) and Clagut(?) Pruggl; a Melchior Matutsch of Burgeis is recorded in 1545 (Marienberg, Stiftsarchiv, Urkunden VI/385), consistent with the first half of the 16th century(?).

content.title: Reuse label
content.description: Label 'Der diener und Ehalten Gedinng 1550' in display script, from the strip's reuse as a wrapper; whether it was written at the time of reuse is not established.

identification: Latin notarial instrument, probably part of the width only and almost entirely faded; a binding of 'Hs 23' until 1965 according to a modern pencil note; only 'In Nomine domini Amen. Anno a Natiuitate(?)' is read; parties, place and date unread
note: The opening 'In Nomine d(omi)ni Amen. Anno a Natiuitate(?)' is read on canvas 0; line 1 does not run on into line 2, so the leaf is probably a vertical piece of a wider instrument and the dating clause probably cut away as well as faded. A modern pencil note on the back, read as 'bis 1965 als Einband in Hs 23', and a pencilled 'Hs 23' on the mounted typed slip (1964 or later) say the leaf was a binding of manuscript 23. Red, green, blue, saturation, blue/red ratio and principal-component contrasts were tried: word shapes consistent with the slip's 'principe et domino domino', 'et Tirolis', 'Romanorum imper', 'regnorum' and 'constitutus egregius' show, but all were read with the slip in view and none is confirmed independently. No party, place or date was read, so no search could be directed; a description of Hs 23 was not reachable (manuscripta.at down).

content.title: Unidentified notarial instrument
content.description: About 40 long lines, almost entirely faded. Inc.: In Nomine domini Amen. Anno a Natiuitate(?) ... Probably only part of the width of the original survives.
content.remarks: Later 15th or 16th century on the hand. A modern pencil note on the back, read as 'bis 1965 als Einband in Hs 23', says the leaf was a binding of manuscript 23. A typed partial transcription of 1964 or later is mounted with it. Parties, place and date are not read.

identification: Two adjacent strips from a German parchment charter of the sixteenth century (year begins 'fünff-', rest lost), its first line in display script: a religious house ('vnnsers Gotshaus', probably Stams) grants to [...]ragne[r?] and his wife Maria and their heirs a farm with pieces formerly of, or belonging to, the Maratschhof, bounded by Wonhofer's Prunnwisl(?), the common way and other neighbours, probably in hereditary tenancy ('[..]bs Paurecht(?)'), for yearly dues including three Shrovetide hens, ten eggs(?) and a heriot (Todfall)
note: The strips were read line by line on the image: an opening line in display script '[...]nbs vnd Im ober[.]n [.]nntal' (the n may be an m with its first stroke cut), 'Vnnsers. Gotshaus [Vr?]bar', the grantees '[...]ragne / vnnd Maria / seiner Eelichen', bounds naming '[..]rt Wonhofers Prunnwisl(?)' and 'Hannß Hebs[..]chers', land 'vormalts Maratschhofs' and 'in dise[n/r] Marätschhof', '(Coherennzen(?)) / Gelegenhait(?)', '[..]bs Paurecht(?) / den benanten hof', dues 'drei Fasnachthennen / Zehen Ayr(?)' and 'ainen Todtfal', and '[..]nd Seligmachers [G]eburdt fünff='. Layout and formulas are compatible with Stams abbots' grants of 1573 and 1578 for Marling (Marienberg, Stiftsarchiv, Urkunden XXI/169 and XXI/171, compared on the images); those features are generic and neither charter has the 'obern Inntal' wording, so Stams is the probable issuer by inference only, and 'Coherennzen', 'Gelegenhait' and 'Paurecht' are reconstructions that still need an independent reading. Tarneller places the Maratschhof and the Wonhof on the Töll near Meran and records Stams lordship of the Maratschhof only for 1633; a Michael Hebsteckh and a Sigmund Jäger 'genannt Marätscher', both of Plars, appear in a Wilten charter of 1584. No record of this grant was found by searching monasterium.net (Stams fonds listing for 1494-1600; site search for the farm and place names), the charter named on the modern label (Lade O XXXIV n. 21, 22 October 1576) is not listed there, and Lebersorg's chronicle pp. 540-541 and 581 could not be read; issuer, surname, rent and year are lost, no human review. Another Stams fragment, F-g1bu (1575), names the same farm.

content.title: Grant of a farm tied to the Maratschhof
content.description: A religious house ('vnnsers Gotshaus', probably Stams) grants to [...]ragne[r?], his wife Maria and their heirs a farm bounded by Wonhofer's Prunnwisl (?), the common way and other neighbours and tied to the Maratschhof, probably in hereditary tenancy ('[..]bs Paurecht' (?)), for yearly dues including three Shrovetide hens, ten eggs (?) and a Todfall. The first line is in display script; the year begins 'fünff-' and the rest is lost.
content.remarks: The issuer, the grantee's surname, the rent and the year are lost. Layout and formulas are compatible with Stams abbots' grants of 1573 and 1578 (Marienberg, Stiftsarchiv, Urkunden XXI/169 and XXI/171). The Maratschhof lies on the Töll near Meran (Tarneller, Die Hofnamen im Burggrafenamt).

identification: Pieces 176-1 and 176-2: German guardianship account (Raitung) of the guardians Oswald Streyler and Pauel Brutsch[..](?), naming Peter Brutsch and his brothers and the children left by the late Hanns(?) G[...](?) zu [St/M]a[u/n]dach(?) (possibly Staudach), taken before the authority at Stams on 7 March 1575(?), with closing balances; 176-3: estate (Verlassenschaft) docket, 15[..]; 176-4: Latin chapter summary of the Life of B. Hermann, monk of Himmerod, following the chapter division of the Life as printed in Chrysostomus Henriquez, Fasciculus sanctorum ordinis Cisterciensis (Brussels 1623), book I, distinctio 12, chapters 1-4
note: 176-1r reads '[O]swalden Streyler auch / Pauel Brutsch[..](?) al[s] / Gerhaben vnnd Pet[er] / Brutschen vnd seiner / gebrueder Raitung / weillennd Hanns(?) G[...](?) / zu Staudach(?) seligen ver- / lassen Khinder' and 'Von der Obrigkhait zu Stambs am 7 tag Martij a(nn)o 1575(?)'; 176-2r closes the account ('Also bleiben die Brutschen den Kindern vätterlichs ... noch schuldig 76 fl 22') and dates one receipt 'a(nn)o / 75', which supports but does not secure the year. the place is possibly Staudach; the deceased father's surname is not read, and the docket 176-3r is read only as 'Hanndlung zwischen [..] Christls(?) seligen(?) wittib(?) vnd khin[der](?) Verlassenschafft 15[..]'. The Latin strip 176-4 numbers its entries 'Cap. 2', '3.', '4.' and follows chapter by chapter the Vita Beati Hermani Monachi Hemenrodensis in Henriquez's Fasciculus (1623, pp. 220-223, read on the page images at https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb10940071?page=224): the Child Jesus at his Mass (c. 1), demons seen in choir and a demon beside a tippling monk (c. 2), two brothers who drive off the spirit of fornication by the words taught by their 'Confessarius' Hermann (c. 3), and the monk long tempted after the gaze of a nun (c. 4); it is a reader's summary, not the printed wording; Henriquez says he compiled the Life himself (p. 231, 'vitam eius ... in hunc modum collegi'), so the summary was made from his book, after 1623 (the 1631 edition was not checked). A blind reader confirmed 'Assidet demon bib..', 'Qui instruend..', 'subditi', 'fratres', 'fornica..' and 'Hermanni'. No outside record of the account was found (Google Books, Internet Archive full text); monasterium.net was not consulted.

content.persons: Oswald Streyler; Pauel Brutsch[..](?); Peter Brutsch
content.description: Account of the guardians of the children left by the late Hanns(?) G[...](?) zu Staudach(?), naming Peter Brutsch and his brothers, taken before the authority at Stams on 7 March 1575(?), with the closing balances owed by the Brutsch brothers to the children.

content.title: Docket on an estate (Verlassenschaft), 15[..]
Chapter summary of the Life of B. Hermann, monk of Himmerod
content.description: Numbered summaries (Cap. 2, 3, 4): the Child Jesus present at his Mass; demons seen in choir; two brothers who drive off the spirit of fornication by the precept of their confessor Hermann; a monk long tempted by the gaze of a nun.
content.remarks: Follows the chapter division and content of the Vita as printed in Henriquez, Fasciculus sanctorum ordinis Cisterciensis (Brussels 1623), I, dist. 12, c. 1-4 (pp. 220-223), whose matter comes from Caesarius of Heisterbach; a summary in the reader's own words, made from Henriquez or his source, probably after 1623.

identification: Sermones Amici (anonymous collection of preaching distinctions in alphabetical order): Amicus II and Ascendere I on one leaf (45v cols 3-4, 45r cols 1-2), Converti on the other (45r cols 3-4, 45v cols 1-2)
note: The strip is the head of a paper bifolium with the first four lines of eight columns, all reread on the images; they agree in wording and order with the 1501 Basel print Sermones Amici ex corrupto reintegrati, read on Munich page images (bsb10990936, scans 9-10 and 16-17): the end of the second distinction on Amicus and the start of Ascendere on one leaf, four passages of Converti on the other. Small differences from the print include meam for nostram, coronet for coronaret, asina for asino, avertimus for advertimus and respiro for spero, and two words in 45v col. 4 remain uncertain. The Ash Wednesday sermon of Conrad of Saxony (Peltier vol. 13, pp. 142-143, compared in machine-read text only) is a parallel to the Converti distinction, and where the two differ the fragment has the wording of the Sermones Amici. The print names no author and the collection's authorship was not investigated; no human review.

fragmentarium.title: Sermones Amici
fragmentarium.subtitle: Distinctions Amicus II, Ascendere I, Converti

content.title: Sermones Amici, distinctions Amicus II and Ascendere I
content.description: First leaf of the bifolium, opening lines of each column. Inc. (45v col. 3): [Spiritus] quidem promptus est caro autem infirma. Unde conformans se. Expl. (45r col. 2): Ecce ancilla domini fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum. Ancilla perfecte.

content.title: Sermones Amici, distinction Converti
content.description: Second leaf, opening lines of each column. Inc. (45r col. 3): nos insequeris tenes et abiiceris. Expl. (45v col. 2): exacerbabitur pater immanitate sceleris mei mitigabitur in.
content.remarks: The passage has a parallel in Conrad of Saxony's fifth sermon for Ash Wednesday (printed among the works of Bonaventure); the fragment's wording is that of the Sermones Amici.
