identification: Tabula super Summam confessorum, the alphabetical index printed with Johannes de Friburgo, Summa confessorum: entries Impedimentum (end), Inquisitio, Insidie, Institutio, Interdictum; Lyon 1518 edition, tabula fol. xv recto-verso
note: A research reader reread all four strips on both sides on the native images and compared them with page images of the index in the Lyon 1518 edition of the Summa confessorum: they agree entry for entry, in wording, order and question numbers (Inquisitio q. vi-vij; Interdictum q. ccxxxij-ccxxxiiij and ccxlj-ccxlix, book III title 33), and the letter 'e' after the numbers is the usage explained in the index's prologue. Small differences from the print include 'audiri possint' for 'possunt' and 'appellat' for 'appellaret'. The side labelled 01v is the recto. Only one printed edition was used, most lines were read with the print open, and who compiled the index was not checked.

content.title: Tabula super Summam confessorum (the alphabetical index printed with Johannes de Friburgo, Summa confessorum)
content.description: Four strips of one leaf. 01v (the recto): end of Impedimentum; Inquisitio, Insidie, Institutio, opening of Interdictum. 01r (the verso): Interdictum, with references to questions 232-234 and 241-249 of book III, title 33.
content.remarks: Agrees entry for entry with the index in the Lyon 1518 edition of the Summa confessorum, fol. xv. The compiler of the index was not established.

identification: Lumen anime (C-type text), Marian chapters, §§474-475 and 480-481 (ed. Harris 2007)
note: A torn single-column scrap. Canvas 1 has 'Anshelmus in sermone ... turris fortitudinis contra demonem', 'Gilbertus de secretis mulierum: Mulier debilis et infirma sepe speculum quod inspicit visibus suis ipsius frangit' and 'Constantinus', in the order of Harris's C text, §§480-481; canvas 0 has the theme of §474 and the §475 rubric 'Alkabicius in theorica planetarum: [Cu]ncti quidem planete'. A research reader reread both faces on the images and compared them with Harris using Google Books snippets only (page images not seen); differences include 'tu perimis'/'occidis et perimis' and 'ipsius'/'ipsa'. At §474 the fragment's 'Athanasius in sermone: Dudum in inuicem tam celi quam terre ruisset machina ...' is not in Harris's index there; the same sentence stands in the 1518 Augsburg print of version A attributed to 'Orosius super cant.' (MDZ page image), so it may be a variant application and authority, but Harris's Latin §474 was not seen, so the comparison at §474 is unresolved. Version B and C manuscripts were not consulted; the 'verify' link opens the Google Books search that shows the §480-481 snippet, the best match, since the MDZ print shows only the variant §474 sentence.

fragmentarium.title: Lumen anime
fragmentarium.subtitle: Version C, §§474-475, 480-481

content.title: Lumen anime (version C), Marian chapters
content.description: 01r: §474, Mary compared to the firmament, with an authority 'Athanasius in sermone', and the rubric of §475, Alkabicius in theorica planetarum: [Cu]ncti quidem planete. 01v: end of §480 (Anshelmus in sermone: Tu auctor salutis mee) and §481 (Gilbertus de secretis mulierum: Mulier debilis et infirma ...).
content.remarks: The §474 quotation 'Dudum in inuicem tam celi quam terre ruisset machina' is given to 'Orosius super cant.' in the Augsburg 1518 print of version A; its relation to Harris's §474 is open.

bibliography: N. Harris, The Light of the Soul: The Lumen anime C and Ulrich Putsch's Das liecht der sel (Oxford 2007), pp. 353, 356

identification: Contents leaf (41_2r) and binding (41_1) of a lost volume of Latin orations, probably from the Ingolstadt university milieu in or after the 1560s: two entries carry the titles of Ingolstadt prints (Paulus Lignarius, Oratio de vita et laudibus Ulpiani, 1564; Johannes Albertus Wimpinensis, Oratio de fine philosophiae, 1561) and one is addressed to an abbot 'D. Neupeck', perhaps Georg Neupeck of Scheyern; the reverse (41_2v) carries an unidentified zodiac allegory of Christ as the Sun that quotes Manilius, Astronomica V.140-143, and Silius Italicus, Punica I.257-258
note: The contents list on 41_2r (canvas 0) names some twenty orations and poems with struck and replaced folio numbers. Two entries carry the titles of orations printed at Ingolstadt by the Weissenhorn brothers, compared on the title pages: Paulus Lignarius, Oratio de vita et laudibus Ulpiani (1564, VD16 L 1734) and Johannes Albertus Wimpinensis, Oratio de fine philosophiae et quomodo ad ipsum perveniri liceat (1561, VD16 A 1269); if the list is out of folio order there, the second fills fol. 39-50 (the 50 is this reading; it could be taken for 90), the number of leaves the catalogue gives for the print, but the first fills 4 leaves against the 8 the catalogue gives, so whether the lost volume held prints or manuscript copies is open. 'Oratio in Dominum D. Neupeck Abbatem' perhaps means Georg Neupeck, abbot of Scheyern, named in two books of the Ingolstadt professor Gamerius (OCR only). The 21 lines of prose on 41_2v (canvas 1) take the Sun through Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo and Scorpius as an allegory of Christ ('ipse Virgo natus ex uirgine') and quote Manilius V.140-143 word for word as printed at Lyon in 1551 ('certantes lucis ad oras Pleiades ducit ... in lucem educunt') and Silius Italicus, Punica I.257-258 ('flammiferis tellus radiis cum exusta dehiscit, candentique globo medius coquit aethera fervor'; Silius from a transcription, not a page). The oration was not found by phrase searches in the Munich digital library and Google Books; the paper slip in the cover is only a caption for the list and the spine label is illegible.

fragmentarium.title: Contents leaf and binding of a volume of Latin orations, two of them printed at Ingolstadt (1561, 1564)

content.title: Contents list of a volume of Latin orations
content.description: Orations on the Christmas vigil, the life and praise of Ulpian, the study of law, philosophy and good letters, wedding orations, 'in Mortem Imperatoris', 'in funere Maximiliani Imperatoris', funeral orations and poems, and 'Oratio in Dominum D. Neupeck Abbatem', with folio numbers.
content.remarks: 'Oratio de Vita et laudibus Vlpiani' and 'Oratio de fine Philosophiae, et quomodo ad ipsum peruenire licet' agree, but for spelling ('Vlpiani', 'peruenire licet' for 'perueniri liceat'), with the titles of orations by Paulus Lignarius (Ingolstadt 1564) and Johannes Albertus Wimpinensis (Ingolstadt 1561). Neupeck is perhaps Georg Neupeck, abbot of Scheyern. The volume is lost; whether it held prints or manuscript copies is not known.

content.title: Oration with an allegory of Christ as the Sun in the zodiac
content.description: The Sun runs through the signs from Aries to Scorpius; each sign is applied to Christ ('ipse Virgo natus ex uirgine').
content.remarks: Quotes Manilius, Astronomica V.140-143, in the 16th-century printed text, and Silius Italicus, Punica I.257-258. Not identified.

identification: Ten paper leaves: (175-9r) a German account leaf carrying the reddish offset of Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 120 verso (F-53hg: Galen, Ad Glauconem, old Latin version, book II, on scirrhus and the fats), which lay against it; (175-1, 175-2) 17th-century Latin lecture notes on the prologue question of theology (Aquinas ST I q. 1), source not found; (175-3 to 175-10) German administrative papers of the 17th century (a report naming 'dises Landtgerichts Stainach(?)' and the year 1649, endorsements, accounts), not regested
note: The reddish set-off on 175-9r, read from an image flipped top to bottom, is the offset of the verso of Stams, Frg. 120 (F-53hg, the old Latin Galen, Ad Glauconem II, on scirrhus and the fats): it matches that leaf line for line with the same line ends ('feculenta quasi in lapide c(on)string-', 'sebu(m) deinde taurinu(m) sic uitulinu(m)', '[De] adipib(us)', 'leopardinu(m)'), in the same Caroline script, leaf size and line pitch, and Frg. 120 verso carries the mirror offset of 175-9r's German account entries, so the two leaves lay face to face. Leaves 175-1 and 175-2 carry lecture notes on theology (its necessity for salvation, 'Articulus Nonus. An Theologia sit dignior alijs scientijs', the objections of heretics); phrase searches in the Munich digital library and Google Books found no source. Modern pencil notes on those leaves read 'aus Urbar IX/66 vom J. 1641/49'. The German papers include a report naming 'dises Landtgerichts Stainach(?)' and the year 1649 (5r) and an endorsement of 26 January 162[5?] (3r); none is regested.

fragmentarium.title: Theology lecture notes; administrative papers, one with the offset of Stams Frg. 120 (Galen, Ad Glauconem)

content.title: Lecture notes on theology (Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I, q. 1)
content.description: Articles on whether theology is necessary for salvation, whether it is a habit distinct from faith, 'An Theologia sit dignior alijs scientijs' (Articulus Nonus, citing S. Thomas, art. 5), and an article answering the objections of heretics to theology.
content.remarks: Source not identified. Modern pencil notes on both leaves: 'aus Urbar IX/66 vom J. 1641/49'.

content.title: Offset of Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 120 verso (Galen, Ad Glauconem, old Latin version, book II: on scirrhus and the fats)
content.description: Reddish offset, legible in an image flipped top to bottom: [in]doctis medi[cis ... intel]legendo mo[x] ... tali humore locali ... feculenta quasi in lapide c(on)string[it] ... temperata et dicuntur mala[ctica] ... adipesque omnes et sebu[m] ... sebu(m) deinde taurinu(m) ... [De] adipib(us) ... leopardinu(m).
content.remarks: Matches the verso of Frg. 120 (F-53hg) line for line, with the same line ends; Frg. 120 verso carries the mirror offset of the German account entries on this page, so the two leaves lay face to face.

content.title: Administrative papers
content.description: A report to a government body naming 'dises Landtgerichts Stainach(?)' and the year 1649 (5r), an endorsement of 26 January 162[5?] (3r), and accounts.

bibliography: Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 120 (Fragmentarium F-53hg)

identification: Two paper strips of Latin sermon or meditation notes on the love of God and grace, citing Chrysostom (Homily 1 on 2 Timothy, freely), the Opus imperfectum in Matthaeum (homily 32, freely) and Augustine ('Aug. de praeceptis leue est a[...]', probably 'Omne praeceptum Dei leve est amanti', Prosper, Sententiae 222); the notes themselves are unidentified
note: The margin note signed 'Chrysost.' ('sicut ignis lignis sic gratia alacritate et desiderio indiget') gives the sense of Chrysostom, Homily 1 on 2 Timothy, section 2 (on 2 Tim 1:6), compared on the page in the Latin of the Paris edition of 1835-1839 ('Ut enim ignis opus habet lignis, sic et gratia alacritate nostra'); a 16th-century Latin version (Alardus 1539, OCR only) has 'ignis indiget lignis', closer to the strip. The sentence 'nec terra sine pluuia fert fructus, sic nec gratia sine uoluntate nec uoluntas sine gratia' freely renders the Opus imperfectum in Matthaeum, homily 32 (same edition, p. 873, read on the page). The confidence is for these cited sentences, not for the notes. The Augustine citation is probably 'Omne praeceptum Dei leve est amanti' (Prosper, Sententiae 222, headed 'De praecepto Dei'), on three words and the heading. The main prose ('Quando ergo res sic se habet, quid causae est. quia non amant, non desiderant') was not found by Google Books, Internet Archive, MDZ or CoMMA searches, nor in Lohner's Bibliotheca manualis concionatoria or Alardus's Selectae similitudines (OCR text). A modern pencil note on both strips says they come from an archival item IX/66 of 1641/49; the versos carry no early text.

fragmentarium.title: Notes on the love of God and grace

content.title: Sermon or meditation notes on the love of God and grace
content.description: Cites Augustine ('Aug. de praeceptis leue est a[...]'), in a marginal note Chrysostom ('sicut ignis lignis sic gratia alacritate et desiderio indiget'), and the comparison of grace and will with rain and earth.
content.remarks: The marginal note freely renders Chrysostom, Homily 1 on 2 Timothy (on 2 Tim 1:6); the rain and earth sentence freely renders the Opus imperfectum in Matthaeum, homily 32. The Augustine citation is probably 'Omne praeceptum Dei leve est amanti' (Prosper, Sententiae 222). The notes are not identified. A modern pencil note says the strips come from an archival item IX/66 of 1641/49.

identification: Binding waste of five paper pieces: cancelled fifteenth-century rent and delivery notes with a first-person memorandum dated Saturday before St Lucy (11 December) [14]62, and fragments of seventeenth-century German letters (a postscript about rents to 'Euer Gnaden', line-ends mentioning the Regierung, an address leaf to 'Walther V[..]'); issuers and receiving house not named
note: On canvas 0, piece 169-3r carries a cancelled first-person memorandum about deliveries and a dispute (flax, lard, fish) ending '[sams]tag vor lucie do ... dz selbm anno lxij ... dec[em]br(is)(?)', and short cancelled receipt entries such as 'It(em) [W?]al[t?]h[..](?) vo(n) A[ltdorff](?) pracht an dornstag vor barbare XX metze fesen', with rye, barley and spelt in Metzen. The word check confirmed 'lxij' (the blind readers' 'xvij' is l+x misread) and 'samstag vor lucie', and marked the month word, the person's name ('-aur' is not on the crop) and the place (only the initial A/O is visible) as uncertain. Only 'lxij' is written, so the century is supplied from the fifteenth-century hand; a modern pencil '1462 dec.' agrees. Saturday before Lucy 1462 is 11 December (Julian), and Thursday before Barbara 2 December if the same year holds. The other pieces are seventeenth-century Kurrent letter fragments, and a modern pencil note says the pieces came from the binding of Stams Urbar IV/42 of 1625. No searches were made for these private notes and letters, and monasterium.net was not checked. No issuer, receiving house or complete regest is established for any piece, so it stays partial; no human review.

content.title: Cancelled rent and delivery notes
content.description: A first-person memorandum about deliveries of flax, lard and fish and a dispute, dated Saturday before St Lucy [14]62 (11 December), and cancelled receipt entries for rye, barley and spelt in Metzen.
content.remarks: Issuer and receiving house not named.

content.title: Fragments of letters
content.description: A postscript about rents to 'Euer Gnaden', line-ends mentioning the Regierung, and an address leaf to 'Walther V[..]'.

identification: Two unrelated German paper pieces: (1) strip of a guardianship settlement for the child of a deceased '[..]ädling(?)', with interest from Candlemas [15]78 to Candlemas [15]79; (2) folded sheet listing provisions issued at kreuzer prices to named men 'and their workmates', with Latus totals, undated; issuers lost
note: On canvas 0 the strip (172-1) was read on the image: '[..]ädling selige(?) Khind', the maternal estate ('Müetterlich Guet', 5 fl 22 kr), the paternal third ('Vätterlich ... In ligenden vnnd farennden sein dritten tail', 76 fl 52 kr) and a sale at '[Perg?]khofen', 'Summa 84 fl 3 lb 8 k', deductions for the guardian's costs leaving 'Bleibt Jr noch schuldig 80 fl 6 k', interest 'von Liechtmeß 78 biß auf Liechtmeß 79' of 3 fl 15 kr, and the child's third of a dispute cost, with the sums checking arithmetically. The word check confirmed both Liechtmeß years and both headings, and corrected the first reading's '[...]dlin seligs Khind' to '[..]ädling selige(?) Khind', so the deceased's name remains unresolved. The century of 78/79 is supplied from a modern pencil 'ao. 1579' on the strip's verso and the Kurrent script, not written; the same pencil may assign the strip to a different binding than the catalogue's IVa/F,5, which is unresolved. The sheet (172-2) is read securely as a priced list of salt, Brein, rice, oil, brandy, vinegar, honey, nails, lead, cabbage and wine issued to named men, but carries no issuer, occasion or date. No outside record was sought for these private accounts. The parties' names and the sheet's occasion are not established, so it stays partial; no human review.

content.title: Guardianship settlement for the child of the late [..]ädling(?)
content.description: Maternal and paternal estate of the child, with deductions for the guardian's costs, leaving 80 fl 6 kr owed, and interest from Candlemas [15]78 to Candlemas [15]79.

content.title: List of provisions
content.description: Salt, Brein, rice, oil, brandy, vinegar, honey, nails, lead, cabbage and wine issued at kreuzer prices to named men 'and their workmates', with Latus totals. Undated.

identification: Stams abbey, register of reckonings (Raittungen) with servants, tenants and officials, 1538: master Petter the sawyer (2 M[a]y(?)-15 Sept 1538), a ferryman (12 Sept) and Michl Ferg the ferryman (7 Nov 1538), Michl Salgeber, Amtmann at Fliess (7 Nov 1538), Sabina, widow of Frantz Vischmayster, the lord of Stams's Marstaller (8 Oct 1538), and one account with heading lost; four leaves, one numbered 92
note: Six reckonings in one German Kurrent hand, read on the image; the sums on 3r, 4r, 1r and 3v were recomputed and agree, while the 4v grain totals are not reconciled; the abbey is named in the text ('meins gnedigen herrn von Stambs', 'Paul von Stams'). An independent reader read the lower half of 4v, where the closing grain figures are the total Salgeber delivered against the 1537 yield (rye 1[7?]0, barley 29 = 15 plus a later addition of 14), not a balance. The names and headings given to blind word-check readers held when adjudicated on the image, including 'zu Flies', where both blind readers had read a P; on the year both had leaned to 1578, and the coordinator reread the three year crops and found the period's z-shaped 3, giving 1538, which agrees with the account's own references to the 1537 yield and the rent for 1538. Not read or uncertain are the month of the sawyer's start (probably May; the capital M was not resolved by an independent review), the year of the 12 September reckoning, the name on 2r and two names on 3v; a modern pencil note names the host volume (Stams II/G 34, 1586), and no outside record of the entries is known.

content.title: Raittungen of Stams Abbey, 1538
content.persons: Petter, Sagmaister; Michl Ferg; Michl Salgeber; Sabina, widow of Frantz Vischmayster
content.description: Six reckonings: with master Petter the sawyer (2 May (?) to 15 September 1538), a ferryman (12 September) and Michl Ferg the ferryman (7 November 1538), Michl Salgeber, Amtmann at Fliess (7 November 1538), Sabina, widow of Frantz Vischmayster, Marstaller of the lord of Stams (8 October 1538), and one with the heading lost.
content.remarks: Four leaves, one numbered 92.

identification: Mathias Heckhen of Mils (Herrschaft Thaur), court-appointed guardian, second guardianship account for Ursula, daughter of the late Oswald Geissler of Mils and wife of Martin Vischler of Absam, running from 24 August 1637; closing clause, copy issued to the husband, dated 1 July [16]39 (century supplied from the 1637 start date); opening and closing pages only
note: Guardian, ward, parents, husband, action, places and both dates are read on the image; the closing year is written 'Neununddreissig' without a century, which is supplied from the account's own 'Sechzehenhundert Sibenunddreissigisten' (1637) on 1v. An independent reader reread the closing (2v) and 1v on the image before seeing the research transcription and agreed; blind word-check readers, adjudicated on the image, confirmed the years, Heckhen, Oswald Geissler and Vischler, and the husband's forename is 'Mart-/in' across a line break. Uncertain: the mother's surname Lindtnerin(?), the second witness's surname (Rotlass?), and whose seal authenticated the copy; the 2r balance (21 fl 17 kr) was read only once. The coordinator read no passage beyond the word check and the independent reread; no outside record of the act is known.

identification: Strips of a German parchment deed of sale, dated in a year probably ending '[...]ssigisten Jar' (a year in the thirties; by the script probably 1530-1539): an agent ('procurator') of the late Anna Hornpa[ch..] sells for himself and his heirs a property bounded by holdings of Conrad [.]haller and of a Perger; buyer, object, day and place lost
note: On canvas 0 three adjacent strips and a fourth below carry 'fur mich Vnnd all mein', 'procura|tor weiland Anna | Hornpa[ch..]', '[v]nnsern(?) Gnedigen(?) Erb(?) vnd Zinßherren', the boundaries 'mittag an Co|nrad [.]hallers' (blind: 'Con|rad thallers') and 'Vnd an h[..]n | pergers guet', and on the lower strip 'Das kauff[..]', 'mein Erben' and, as the last written line, '[...]ssigisten Jar', probably the end of the dating clause (a blind reader of a crop without the modern pencil note read '[.]ugiſtn' and a large looped capital with 'a..r', compatible but not decisive): a year in the thirties of its century, by the script probably 1530-1539. The pencil '(1530)' beneath it is a modern note that agrees with this but was not used. Stams charters on monasterium.net record a Hornbach family at Flaurling (K_IV_23, 6 January 1540; Heins Hornpacher, 1599/1600), a name lead only; no matching regest of the 1530s was found there by word search. Buyer, object and day are lost.

content.description: The procurator of the late Anna Hornpa[ch..] sells, for himself and his heirs, a property bounded by holdings of Conrad [Pf/Sch]aller and of a Perger. The dating clause ends '[...]ssigisten Jar', a year in the thirties, by the script 1530-1539.
content.remarks: Buyer, object, day and place are lost.

identification: Two unrelated paper pieces from the 1625 urbar binding: (173_1) end of a German act sealed with the secret seal of the abbey of Stams, given at Stams on 29 May 1560(?) (decade word damaged), action and beneficiary lost; (173_2) part of a Latin petitionary letter to a 'Venerande in Christo Pater' (probably the abbot) on behalf of two fathers named Iohannes and their sons Michael Bu[c]her and one Gla[...], sender and date lost
note: On piece 1 the corroboration and dating clause were read on the image: '... nach des Lanndtsrecht . Vngeuarlich . Diß zu warem vrkhundt haben wir vnser Abbtey Secreth Innsigl hiefurgedruckht . Geben in ob[ge]melten vnserm Gotshaus Stambs . am Neün vnnd zwainzigisten tag . Monats Maij . Anno ⁊c Im funfft- [...] vnd Sech[t]zigisten(?)'. Two fresh readers and an adjudicator confirmed Stambs, 'Neün' (ruling out 'Ain', 21 May), 'Maij' and 'Im funfft-'; the decade word is damaged, only '...h(t)z i...' is legible, so 'Sech-' is not secure and 'Acht-' is not excluded, and 'fünfzehenhundert' rests on 'funfft-' plus an illegible word. The year 1560 (29 May, a Wednesday in the Julian calendar if so) is therefore a probable reading that agrees with, but does not rest on, the modern pencil note '29. Mai 1560' on the piece. On piece 2 the Latin reads 'Venerunt ad me Iohannes b[u]cher(?) et Iohannes [...] obnixe rogat[...] habuerunt : filios suos michaele(m) bu[c]her et [...] gla[...]', with the purpose lost at the cut; the modern pencil list of names in the margin was not used for the reading. monasterium.net (Stams fonds) has 1560 charters for 19 Feb, 10 Dec and 30 Dec but nothing for 29 May, and Bucher charters only for 1589 and 1595; the abbot's name in 1560 was not established. Partial because the action and parties of piece 1 and the sender and purpose of piece 2 are lost; no human review.

identification: Pupils' writing exercises signed 1675 (Martin Anger, Christianus Bebrl(?)): the main German model text is an abridged and adapted excerpt of Proverbs 4:1-8, closest to Johann Dietenberger's Catholic German Bible among the five Bibles compared, followed by a rhymed Marian exhortation built on the motto 'Zu Gott und unser lieben Frauen setz ich mein Hoffnung und Vertrauen'; also a Latin Magnificat (Luke 1:46-48), an unidentified New Year's address and a copied legal model letter dated internally 15 October 1664 (Oberösterreichische Regierung, plaintiff Sterzinger)
note: Four sheets each carry a model text copied twice, alphabets, numerals and a signed 'Anno ... Jahrzahl' line ('Martin Anger Anno 1675 Jahrzahl' on 3r, 'A. 1. 675' after 'Christianus Bebrl(?)' on 1r); 1664 is only the date inside the copied letter. The German text on 1r and 1v runs 'Meine kinder höret die wort ewrs(?) vatters(?) auf das ihr den rechten verstandt ... überkhomen die weisheit, nimb an, vergiß nit den verstandt vnd weich nit von der röd meines mundts, so wirdt sie dich erhöchen vnd zu grossen ehren bringen', then in rhyme 'Mein kind zu Gott vnd vnser lieben frauen sötz auch dein hoffnung vnd vertrauen ... vnd sonderlichen in vnseren Absterben. Amen'. Two readings are Dietenberger's (Catholische Bibell, Cologne 1564, scan 730) and are in none of the other Bibles compared (Luther, Ulenberg, Eck 1537, Nürnberg 1539): 'den rechten verstand' (4:1) and 'Vberkom die weißheit, Nim an verstand' (4:5). Two phrases of the exercise are not in the 1564 text: 'die wort ewrs vatters' (1564: 'die lere') and 'zu grossen ehren bringen' (1564: 'wirt dich zu ehren machen'); only the 1564 printing of Dietenberger was read. Eck's Bible of 1537 reads 'Besitz die weißhait' and is excluded on the page, and a Nürnberg 1539 Proverbs also has 'Vberkum die weyßheit'. The opening couplet of the Marian lines is a Catholic motto found in print, as 'Zu Gott vnd vnser lieben Frawen setz ich mein Hoffnung vnd Vertrawen' in the Fragstuck über den Catechismum Petri Canisii (Ingolstadt 1629, p. 65; by snippet also 1594), and recorded by snippet as a Tyrolean house inscription; the exercise recasts it as an address to the pupil. Partial because the schoolmaster's model joining the two texts was not found, and the New Year's address ('Weillen wür von den Gnaden Gottes dises Neüe Jahr ... angefangen'), the lines beginning 'Gleich wie ain kranckher(?) Mensch' and the legal letter remain untraced after searches of Google Books and MDZ.

identification: German paper register of hospitality kept day by day, Stams area (Upper Inn valley, Tyrol), late sixteenth or early seventeenth century: meals ('mal') and wine given to named visitors, including the parish priests of Telfs and Silz(?), the Pfleger and Richter of Petersberg, tenants (Zinsleute) and messengers; keeper and year not established
note: Item 1 was read on the image on both faces (1r main block, days [19?] to 5 and line-beginnings of a cut column with days 19-22; 1v, days 23-28), with each entry opening 'An dem tag' and the day of the month in the margin, e.g. 'pfarrer von Telffs · 2 · mal geben', 'pfleger vnd Richter von Petersperg ... yedlichem · 2 · mal geben', '· 3 · Zinßleut ain mal geben' and 'hab ime 4 maß wein geben'. The word check confirmed the place names Telffs, P[e/i]tersperg and Rattnberg (Rattenberg, on the strip 2v: 'von Zirl vnd von Rattenberg'); the name after the second 'pfarrer von' carries two dots on its vowel, so it is literally 'Sülz/Sylz' and 'Silz(?)' (where Petersberg lies) keeps its query mark. The recurring 'yedlichem' (to each) and the first-person 'hab ime ... geben' make this a running record of meals actually given rather than a list of dues, though 'yedlichem' is not fully certain. Item 2 is a narrow strip in the same hand whose line-ends closely parallel item 1, perhaps another copy or another month; item 3 has only a few initial letters; the cut columns, 2r and 3r rest on the first reading only. No year or month survives in the text. A modern pencil label on 1v, read on the native image as 'IV/42 vom J. 1625' (the word-check crop had clipped the last digit), records removal from Stams volume IV/42 of 1625; it dates the host volume, not the register. The keeper (abbey office or a private household, possibly a parish priest given 'meinem pfarrer') is not established; no outside record was sought, since a household register of this kind has no reason to be printed, and the Stams finding aid for volume IV/42 was not checked.

content.title: Register of hospitality
content.description: Day-by-day record of meals ('mal') and wine given to named visitors, among them the parish priests of Telfs and Silz (?), the Pfleger and Richter of Petersberg, tenants (Zinsleute) and messengers. Keeper and year not established.
content.remarks: Item 2 is a strip in the same hand with closely parallel entries; item 3 has only a few initial letters.

identification: Three paper scraps: piece 183_1 is a student's excerpt sheet of figures from Virgil, Eclogue 1, copying the anonymous school Annotationes printed with Melanchthon's scholia (closest to the Frankfurt editions of 1561-1587, not Cologne 1620), with Boethius' definition of quaestio; 183_2 has introductory theology notes (natural and supernatural knowledge of God, faith and theology) and a summary of the plan of Aquinas' Summa theologiae, with a list of clothing and belongings, source not found; 183_3 (German sermon draft on humility) is unidentified
note: On 183_1 the verse lines of Ecl. 1.1-2, 1.27, 1.34-35 and 1.68-69 are each followed by their figure note, agreeing note for note with the Annotationes 'In Eclogam I'; 'pro Mantua' and 'fistula avenae culmo facta' without 'ex' are the readings of the Frankfurt family (1561-1587) against Cologne 1620, and no single printing is named. The opening definition 'Quaestio est in dubitationem ambiguitatemque adducta enunciatio(?)' is Boethius (De topicis differentiis I); the 'Definitio nominis ... decem literis' sentence is unplaced. On 183_2 the recto reads 'Sup(er)n(atur)alis rursus dividit(ur) [in fidem et] theologiam proprie dictam. Fides e(st) qua ... eisq(ue) immediate sine discursu assentimus', and the verso 'In 2da agit de motu creaturae r(ation)alis in Deum ... In 3a p(ar)te agit de Christo', a paraphrase of the plan of the Summa theologiae, below a list of clothing and belongings; Google Books, MDZ and Internet Archive searches found no source with this wording. The 183_3 draft was not searched, and a modern pencil note 'aus Einbd.(?) IX/66 v. J. 1641/49' is a host lead only. Partial because the Virgil layer is an excerpted source and the other two pieces have no identified text.

identification: Left-edge strip of a German private deed on parchment, Tyrol, second half of the sixteenth century, issued in the first person with a cadel initial: a conveyance with a buyer ('Khauffer'), a meadow 'genant ...', a lord's consent, a 'Verleichbrief' and a sealing request; issuer, parties, object, place and date lost
note: Only the first one to three words of about 37 lines survive, read on the image on canvas 0: '[M]ichael(?), dab[..] or Sab[..]', 'willigung des', 'Hannsen Mai[r?]', 'wisen genant', 'Khauffman[...]', 'Khauffer, sel[...]', 'en den Khau[ffer?]', '[C?]ammerlannd(?)', 'Verleichbrief[e?]', 'Vnd Fünffzeh[en]', 'meiner Erbe[n]', 'Vleissig pitt[...]' and 'Haller gebr[...]'. The word check confirmed 'Verleichbrief', 'Cammerlannd' (line 18) and 'Haller gebr/gebn[..]' (last line, read on the native image), but left the first letters of line 2 uncertain: the name's initial is hidden by the stem of the cadel, and the next word may begin with d or S. These openings show a sale with a lord's consent and reference to a tenancy grant, so the type is a private conveyance, but nothing of the issuer, beneficiary, property, place or date survives. A modern blue-ink note on the back, 'Urbar / Wass[er]t[u]m(?) 1592', presumably names the urbar the strip bound; it would give a terminus ante quem of 1592 only if right, and its second word is uncertain. No search was possible with no name, place or date to match, and the Stams charter regests on monasterium.net were not checked. The result is partial at low confidence because only the document type is established.

content.remarks: Only the opening words of about 37 lines survive. Modern note on the back: 'Urbar / Wass[er]t[u]m(?) 1592'.

identification: Binder's-waste strips (pieces 1-12) from German pleadings and procedural writings in a Tyrolean civil suit heard before a commission, including the heading of a Triplica, with a date read as 30 June 1635; parties, subject and issuing body not established. Pieces 13-21 are a separate struck-through draft concerning a death, a three-year-old child and a guardianship
note: On strips 1-12 (one 17th-century Kurrent chancery hand) the heading '[T]riplica vnnd Di[...] / N. Anwalthaber der [...] / Contra' was read on 2r, with references to a Duplica, 'Triplicando', an Augenschein and a Rechtstagsatzung on 'Zwainzigisten Augu[sti]' later extended, the 'oberesten Regierung', and commissioners speaking with four assessors and adjoined Beisitzer on 12r ('[.]berhamer, auf Lo(t/ſ)h[..]', 'Stainer(?) zu St[a]nng[..](?)'). Strip 10r gives '...es Lorenzen, dem lesten Juni[j] / [Sech]zehenhundert Funffunddreissig', that is 30 June 1635; the word check corrected the year from 1631 and replaced the earlier 'dem Closter zu[...]' with 'dem lesten Juni[j]', so no monastery is named. The year was read on the text; the red-crayon '(16)35' beside it is a modern note that agrees. Whether 1635 dates the writ or is a date cited in it is not known. Strip 3r cites a past year 'Funffzehenhundert ...' passed 'mit Stillschweigen' (the red-crayon '1580?' is a modern guess), and 4r-5r name 'Wüsstaller(?)' and 'des Voggerischen (or Roggerischen) vertrags'. Searches of Google Books and the Internet Archive for these names found nothing; the Stams litigation files, monasterium.net and the Tiroler Landesarchiv commission files were not checked. Partial because the parties and the object of the suit are not established.

A date reads 'dem lesten Juni[j] [Sech]zehenhundert Funffunddreissig' (30 June 1635).

identification: Two German drafts (Konzepte) in one hand, each on its own leaf, probably reports from officials at Hall in Tirol (possibly the salt-office officials) to the prince's Kammer: (1) leaf 1, headed 'Durchl: Camer(?)', advising the purchase for 200 or at most 225 fl of what one 'Hofh.' holds by inheritance, probably in the 'Salzperg(?)'; dating clause incompletely read (possibly day 23; month and year unread); (2) leaf 2, with a heading read 'Den Tirolischen Camer(?)', following a 'beratschlagung vnnd Visitierung' at Hall and concerning the Pfannhaus; writers unnamed, year not established
note: Leaf 1 (1r then 1v) is one draft and leaf 2 (probably 2v then 2r) the other. Leaf 1 opens 'Gnedig herrn. Wellichermassen E: g:', speaks of the prince in the third person ('Innamen der F: Dt: Vnnsers gnedigisten herrn'), has 'Salzperg' in an insertion (read by the research reader and a checker; a blind reader of that crop did not confirm it), answers a petition ('Supp:') sent on for 'gehorsamben bericht', names the sums 200, 225 and 275 fl, and ends with a dating clause read 'Dat. den 23(?) tag', month and year unread (a 7-like sign at the torn corner may be a later mark); leaf 2 opens 'Wolgeborn p.', mentions men sent 'alherab gen Hall. Von wegen beratschlagung vnnd Visitierung', and names the 'Pfanhaus' twice. The two headings carry the same word, read 'Camer(?)' (leaf 1 'Durchl: Camer', leaf 2 'Den Tirolischen Camer'); a blind reader read the leaf-1 heading 'Durch[.]: Camer[.]', with no d, so it is not 'Cardin[al]', but did not confirm the noun on leaf 2 ('D[..] T[.]ri[.]lisch[.] C[.]ij[..]r', low confidence); the word after 'Visitierung des' is struck through, and the margin words are read 'Ambtleut(?)' and 'vnd Hall: Ambtl(?)' (not confirmed by a blind reading), so the writers are placed at Hall and only possibly identified as the salt officials. The seller's name ('Hofh.', 'Hofhaim[er](?)'), the thing sold ('Zinsen(?)', less probably 'Eisen(?)', 'vnd drey Viertl ...'), two names on 2v and the month and year are not settled, and no outside record of either act was found; the Innsbruck Kammer copybooks were not checked; no human review.

fragmentarium.title: Two draft reports from officials at Hall in Tirol, probably concerning the saltworks

content.title: Draft report, probably to the prince's Kammer, on a purchase, probably in the Hall salt mine

content.remarks: The writers are at Hall in Tirol, possibly the salt-office officials (margin: 'Ambtleut(?)', not confirmed).

identification: Opening of an unfinished, unsent German letter from an unnamed son to his parents ('Lieber vatter vnd lieber Muter'), with a pen-trial alphabet above; possibly a pupil's exercise letter; writer, addressees, place and date not given
note: Seven lines were read on the image of 01r: 'Mein freuntlichen gruez(?) zuuor Lieber vatter vnd lieber Muter Ich las Euch zwissen Dass Ich frisch vnd gesundt von den gnaden gottes', he would be glad to hear they are healthy too, he asks his father to speak 'mit den herren' about something, and it breaks off at 'vnnd Ich Bitt dich du wellest'. Above stand a large flourished M and a pen-trial alphabet; the verso is blank apart from binding marks, with no address or seal, so the letter was never sent. The word check left the key word after 'vnd von' unread: 'Innsprugen' is disfavoured because the letter after long s is t-like, and 'zu St[er]zin[g]' is only a letter-shape conjecture. The word after 'Ich las dem' is 'Luttern(?)' or 'L/R-ittern' and is not to be taken as Luther. The only dating evidence is a modern pencil note, 'aus dem Einband / von II/G.33 (aus(?) J. 1535)', which gives the host book and its year, not a date on the letter, plus an early-modern German cursive. No outside search was made, since an unsigned private draft gives no name to search by. Partial because the parties, place and date cannot be established.

content.title: Opening of a letter from a son to his parents
content.description: Inc.: Mein freuntlichen gruez (?) zuuor Lieber vatter vnd lieber Muter Ich las Euch zwissen Dass Ich frisch vnd gesundt von den gnaden gottes ... Breaks off at 'vnnd Ich Bitt dich du wellest'. Above, a pen-trial alphabet.
content.remarks: Unfinished and never sent; possibly a pupil's exercise letter. Writer, addressees, place and date are not given.

identification: Scraps of German account sheets, seventeenth century, probably of a Tyrolean estate or monastic administration (Stams not established): a weekly wage list for digging out a ditch dated 19 September 16[3?]9 (1609 possible), payments for woodcutters' wages and firewood, a materials calculation and a 'Summa diser Außgaben fl. 14'; item 3 is an unrelated strip with one cut line of Latin book hand
note: Items 1 and 2 were read on the image: on 180-2v the heading '[...] ad[i] 19 Septembris / [...] außgrab[...] Graben' and weekly wages per worker ('Wochenlohn fl. 2 · 4', '[...]rg Prunner fl. 1 · 6', '[Ab]rahamb fl. 1 · 6', '[...] Schamblechner(?)'); on 2r payments to Andre Wachter, Andre Payr and others with '[...] holtzerlohn' and '[...] holz zum Brennen'; on 1r a calculation of quantities times unit price with braced subtotals; on 1v payments 'Dem Paul [...] Kolman', 'Dem [...] Holzmayster' and 'Summa diser Außgaben fl. 14 [.] 4'. The word check confirmed 'ad[i] 19' but not the year: the third digit is an open lower bowl with an inward curl, read as 3 (5 possible) and not as a closed 0, so the year is given as 16[3?]9. 1609 remains only as an alternative supported by the weekday (19 September 1609 was a Saturday, a usual pay day; 1639 a Monday, 1659 a Friday), which cannot override the letter form. No issuer, office or account title survives, so the attribution to Stams rests on the fragment's place of keeping alone. Item 3 carries one cut line of a gothic book hand on each face, known only from the first reading ('[...]ntatis an[...]'; '[.]i q(ue) d[...] ca[...]'), too little to search. No outside record was sought, since working accounts of this kind are rarely recorded singly.

content.title: Account sheets
content.description: A weekly wage list for digging out a ditch, dated 19 September 16[3?]9, payments for woodcutters' wages and firewood, a calculation of materials and a total 'Summa diser Außgaben fl. 14'.

identification: Corrected working draft of a German Catholic Reform text of about 1580-1630, headed 'Christlicher ... hausarbait(?) welche(?) der beser(?) geist Teufl einem(?) Christen(?) Mannes(?) darbey eingibt': fifteen numbered counsels spoken by the devil to a lay householder, urging lax religious practice; source or author not found
note: One fast Kurrent hand; the heading, items 1-4, 6-8 and 14-15 were read at native size, several heading words are uncertain ('Mannes' or 'Menschen', 'anweiseth' or 'anwendeth') and items 11-13 are largely unread. The devil addresses a lay householder as 'mein liebe Sel': pray little on rising ('du bist schon gesegneth'), 'las ... die Geistlichen Pfaffen vnd Munich beten', think of 'dein hausarbeit', cheat in buying and selling, avoid 'das öffter Beichten vnd ... Communicieren' that 'die Pfaffn vnnd Jesuiter aufbracht', and be 'nit gar zu fromb' (item 15). The mention of the Jesuits fits the dating of the hand (about 1580-1630, an estimate) and excludes only a date before 1540; the leaves run 2r, 2v, 1v, 1r, and deletions and insertions suggest an author composing. No source was found by MDZ, Google Books or Internet Archive phrase searches, so the record is partial on genre and setting.

fragmentarium.title: The devil's counsels to a Christian householder (draft)

content.title: Christlicher ... hausarbait (?) welche (?) der beser (?) geist Teufl einem (?) Christen (?) Mannes (?) darbey eingibt
content.description: Corrected working draft, about 1580-1630. Fifteen numbered counsels spoken by the devil to a lay householder ('mein liebe Sel'), urging lax religious practice: little prayer, leaving prayer to priests and monks, dishonest trade, no frequent confession or communion, 'nit gar zu fromb'. Inc.: Zum Ersten mein liebe sel volge mire ... zu morgens wann du aufstehest, darffst wenig be[ten].
content.remarks: The leaves run in the order 2r, 2v, 1v, 1r. Item 7 names the Jesuits. Source and author not found.

identification: German first-person declaration of his 'Substantia' (possessions and cash for the year) by a religious, probably a Stams monk in pastoral care in a wine parish (possibly Mais or St. Peter near Meran), with his expense account in fl/kr on the back (subtotal 66 fl 26 kr); writer, addressee and date not given; 1668 or later on the book list
note: Under the heading 'Substantia' face 1 lists habits, scapulars, linen, devotional objects (Agnos Dei, a signet ring, rosaries) and books, among them '3ia Parte Concionu(m) Ruraliu(m) D. Vdalrici Neub[ur]ger', Christoph Ulrich Neuburger's Conciones Rurales, whose third part was first printed in 1668. It then states the cash 'an Parschafft überbliben', with 'Säml wein(?)' (collected wine; 'Säml' three times), 'dz Jar hindurch', 'ferdigen(?)' (last year's) wine, and a list read with doubt as 'verkhünd[en](?), H[ochzeit]en(?), beichthören(?), Khr[anckhen](?)', so it is probably a yearly statement by a monk serving a wine-growing parish; Mais or St. Peter near Meran is possible but neither is named on the leaf. Face 2 is his account: 'Doctor Valen[.]iz(?)', 'pro Medic[...]', a bookbinder and sold books (19 fl 40 kr), cloth for shirts, 'postgelt vnd Zeitung', 'bruederschafft einschreibgelt(?)', a scapular, subtotal 66 fl 26 kr, and 35 fl 10 kr against 'färtigen(?) wein'. A modern pencil note records that the strips were pasted in the Lebersorg chronicle as Beilage 75 until November 1965. Lindner's Album Stamsense (snippets only) names the Stams vicars of those parishes after 1668, but no record of this declaration and no writer's name was found.

content.title: Declaration of possessions and yearly cash (Substantia) by a religious, with an expense account
content.description: 01r: his habits, linen, devotional objects and books, among them the third part of Neuburger's Conciones rurales; then the cash left over for the year, with last year's and this year's collected wine. 01v: an account of expenses in fl and kr (subtotal 66 fl 26 kr), with payments to a doctor, for medicine, to a bookbinder, for shirts, post and newspaper, a confraternity and a scapular. Writer, addressee and date are not given; 1668 or later.
content.remarks: The writer was probably a monk of Stams in pastoral care in a wine-growing parish, possibly Mais or St. Peter near Meran; neither place is named. Until November 1965 pasted in the Lebersorg chronicle (modern pencil note).

identification: Four paper pieces of a German sermon or homiletic draft of the 16th or 17th century on temptation and the devil, with David's fall as exemplum, quoting Ps 29:7-8, Ecclus 34:9 ('der weis Man[n]') and 1 Pet 5:8-9 ('Sobrii estote'); the containing work is not identified
note: The fronts of the two larger pieces were read in full: God lets a person be tried so that he learns whether he is strong or weak ('ich würd nit bewögt werden', '[A]vertisti faciem tuam a me', 'Der nit versuecht ist', 'ob er starckh oder'), the devil apparently takes his revenge on God's image ('auch der teüfel ... ahn seiner bildnus rechen(?)'), and the hearers are to be sober and watch ('Sobrij estote &c', 'Cui resiste fortes in f[ide]', so written). Deletions with replacements written above make it probably an autograph draft. The stained backs gave only a few uncertain words, on the flesh and on temptation, and the two narrow strips only letter groups. MDZ and Google Books phrase searches found only the Bible verses in other works, so the record is partial on genre and subject.

content.title: Sermon on temptation and the devil
content.description: With David's fall as exemplum, quoting Ps 29:7-8, Ecclus 34:9 ('der weis Man[n]') and 1 Pet 5:8-9 (Sobrii estote); the devil is apparently said to take his revenge on God's image.
content.remarks: Probably an autograph draft (deletions and interlinear corrections). Possibly for the third Sunday after Pentecost, whose epistle is 1 Pet 5:6-11; no occasion is shown by the pieces. Not identified.

identification: First page of a 17th-century German letter to a 'Wol Edelgeborner Gnediger Herr' (writer, addressee's name, place and date lost), complaining that certain parishioners ('Kirchleuth') under the addressee's jurisdiction and others have presumed to introduce an improper innovation ('vngebürliche Neuerung') at or concerning one Ruprecht Klainhanser (initial K not certain), touching goods entrusted to the addressee, a 'Kay(?): [alt. Chur:] Herrschafft Ri(t)ten(?)' and the town, and asking in neighbourly fashion that it be stopped
note: Face A (43r) was read on the image: a letter in a Kurrent chancery hand written over faint ruled music staves, opening 'Wol Edelgeborner Gnediger Herr' and continuing '... glaubwürdig vorgetragen worden [W]eß(?) gestalt etwelche Kirchleuth Eur Gnedi[gen] Jurisdiction ... vnd andre mehr, sich an[m]assen, bey dem Ruprecht Klainhanser ihr[e] ...', '[..]sen(?) vngebürliche Neuerung', 'Gütter(?) ... Eur Gnedi: anverthraut[en] Kay(?): Herrschafft Ri(t)ten(?) vnd also bey der Statt', '[..]ch gelangt an Eur [Gn]edi: ... Nachbarlich' and '[..] solche vngebür, abschaffen zuelassen'. The word check changed the group name to 'Kirchleuth' (parishioners; the earlier reading and the place-name speculation built on it are withdrawn) and the surname to 'Klainhanser', whose initial K is not certain (alt. A-); 'Ruprecht' and 'bey der Statt' were confirmed, the lordship name 'Ri(t)ten(?)' stays uncertain, and the title before 'Herrschafft' may be 'Kay:' or 'Chur:'. The text breaks off at the cut lower edge after the start of a second paragraph, so signature, place, date and the writer's identity are lost; the formula and hand point to the 17th century, which is not a date. Face B carries only the abraded music layer, with no address or endorsement. Google Books searches under the earlier spelling 'Kleinhanser' (with 'Ruprecht' and place names) found nothing, and monasterium.net and the Tiroler Landesarchiv were not searched. The complaint and the request are established but the writer and date are not, so the record is partial. A later research reader proposed that the letter concerns merchants' goods unloaded ('Khaufmans(?) Güetter ablegen') at Klainhanser's at Oberpinswang near Füssen, with 'Fuehrleuth' (carters) for 'Kirchleuth'; a blind reader of the same crops confirmed none of those words (it read 'Kirch[.]o[f/ſ]', 'Raumung', 'der Jnsassen'), so that reading is not adopted.

content.title: Letter of complaint (first page)
content.description: To a 'Wol Edelgeborner Gnediger Herr': certain parishioners ('Kirchleuth') under his jurisdiction and others have presumed to introduce an improper innovation concerning Ruprecht Klainhanser (?), touching goods entrusted to the addressee, a lordship Ri(t)ten (?) and the town; the writer asks in neighbourly fashion that it be stopped. Writer, place and date lost.

identification: Two Tyrolean account documents in German: (A) a settlement ('Abraittung') of 6 February 1638 with the timber contractors ('Holzwerchs Fürgedinger(n)(?)'), apparently of the Paznaun ('in Pazn-/aun'(?)), several named men including Gotthardt Vonier(?), for timber work done in 1637 for the Pfanhausambt (apparently the Hall salt works), 400 + 300 = 700 fl, with a short 'Provisoner' list; (B) a receipts extract for the last (52nd) week of 1637, including money from a Salzgaden, tolls, Stadlgeld and wood sales, and a contribution list of about twenty named people totalling 34 fl 30 kr
note: Document A (leaves 228_1-2) is titled 'Abraittung mit dem Holz-/werchs Fürgedingern(?) in Pazn-(?)/aun(?) ... vnd Gotthardt / Vonier(?), wegen der ... / Pfanhausambt holz... / ... des 1637: Jars ver-/richten Holzwerchs Arbeiten' and dated '... den: 6 Februarii A(nn)o 38'; it sets 400 fl and a further 300 fl granted ('Summa baider Posten :700: fl') against payments received. The word after 'Holzwerchs', written also in the heading, is read as Fürgedinger(?), probably the Tyrolean term for a contractor who undertakes timber work (seen only in a search snippet, not on a page) and probably not a surname; the men's names other than Gotthardt Vonier(?) are not read, and the reading Paznaun, split over a line break, is not secure. Document B (leaves 228_3-4) is headed 'Extract über die le[t]ste Woch A(nn)o 1637' with receipts 'in der 52 Wochen', 'Auß dem Salzgaden diese Wochen Empfangen 1621 fl 50 kr', a toll, 'Rechengelt'(?), 'Stadlgelt', sold wood ('Holz vnnd Küsten(?) ... 2531 fl 10 kr') and 'Grundt Zinß', and a list of about twenty contributors ending 'Summa :34 fl :30 kr'; its issuing office is not named. No outside record was found (Google Books and Internet Archive full text for Fürgedinger, Paznaun, Pfannhausamt, Vonier); the Hall Salzamt records in the Tiroler Landesarchiv were not consulted.

content.title: Settlement (Abraittung) with timber contractors
content.description: Settlement of 6 February 1638 with the timber contractors (Holzwerchs Fürgedinger (?)), apparently of the Paznaun (?), for timber work done in 1637 for the Pfanhausambt (apparently the salt works at Hall): 400 + 300 = 700 fl, with 300 fl still to pay; with a short list of Provisoner.

content.title: Extract of receipts for the last week of 1637
content.description: Receipts for the 52nd week of 1637, including money from a Salzgaden, tolls, Stadlgeld and wood sales, and a contribution list of about twenty named people totalling 34 fl 30 kr.
content.remarks: The issuing office is not named.

identification: Bundle of about eleven 16th-century Innsbruck government papers used as binding waste. Item 82-12, read in full: original letter of Emperor Maximilian II, Vienna, 21 July 1565, sending (unnamed, probably Innsbruck) officials copies of the marriage agreements of his sisters Barbara and Johanna with the dukes of Ferrara and Florence. The other items are read only in part: a Latin minute of Tuesday 2 March 1535 on royal-Venetian toll talks, possibly from the arbitration congress at Trent (1533-1535); drafts and letters of 1538-1559 on Bregenz serfs, a diet about aid against the 'Erbfeindt' (the Turks, by the usual sense) reported by the commissioners probably Schweikhart von Gundlfingen and Eberhart von Freyberg, a Schaffhausen petition and a Wolkenstein letter; plus a 17th-century label and a modern parish timetable
note: Item 82-12 reads 'Heyrats abreden, so zwischen den Herzogen von Ferrar, vnd Florenz, auch unsern freundtlichen geliebten Schwestern, Barbara vnd Johanna beschlossen worden ist, hiemit abschrifften zue', dated 'Wienn den ainundzwainzigisten tag Julij Anno im fünfundsechzigisten', signed 'Maximilian'; the addressees are not named and the Innsbruck government is an inference. Item 82-2, dated 'M.D.xxxv. Die Martis .2. Martij', opens 'Cum Cl(arissi)mus(?) Arbiter(?) Regius Curam suscepisset loquendi cu(m) Mag(nifi)cis Agent[ibus] Regijs ut datia insolita tollerentur' and concerns the Venetian Dominium, new collectae and the Verona toll on German goods brought 'p(er) Athesim et vall[em] Lagarina(m)'; an Austro-Venetian arbitration with arbiters of both sides sat at Trent in 1533-1535 (according to a thesis by Della Mea, Udine, consulted once and not re-checked), so the minute, whose verso has the royal side's answers ('De Datijs vero respondent Regij'), is possibly from that congress, but no record of this session was found; the drafts 82-5/82-6 (19 April [15]45) name 'Herr S[....]khart von Gundlfingen freyherr' (the initial S, read also by a blind reader, excludes Leonhart; probably Schweikhart, as the last Freiherr von Gundelfingen, d. 1546, known from snippets) vnnd Herr Eberhart von Freyberg Ritter' as royal commissioners reporting on a diet, at a place read '[R]iedling[en](?)', with envoys of a margraviate, counties and towns about 'hilf wider den Erbfeindt' (a Schweikhart von Gundelfingen is attested until 1546 in printed works found by snippet search; no record of the 1545 commission was found); 82-9 (30 March 1545) is addressed to 'Herrn Franncisc[..] ... Ritter, Hauptman zu' a place read 'Rovereyt(?)' or 'Landeg[k](?)'. The other dated items are 82-13 (8 August(?) 1538), 82-7 and 82-8 (20 March 1545, mandate on serfs in the Herrschaft Bregenz), 82-11 (petition about a Lehentrager 'von Schellenberg(?)' and the town of Schaffhausen, endorsed 1545), 82-10 (3 April 155[0 or 6]) and 82-4 (Hanns Freiherr zu Wolkenstein to royal commissioners, docket 26 June [15]59, body unread); the pencil note 'aus Hs 228 (Compl. c. 1646)' on 82-1 is modern, and no outside record of any item was found.

content.title: Maximilian II, letter, Vienna, 21 July 1565
content.persons: Maximilian II; Barbara of Austria; Johanna of Austria
content.description: Maximilian II sends officials (not named, probably the Innsbruck government) copies of the marriage agreements of his sisters Barbara and Johanna with the dukes of Ferrara and Florence, for the homecomings, the household and the execution of the agreements. Vienna, 21 July 1565.

content.title: Minute of toll negotiations, 2 March 1535
content.description: The royal arbiter reports on his talks with the royal agents about 'datia insolita' and new collectae; the Venetian Dominium on the Verona toll on German goods brought by the Adige and the Lagarina valley; on the verso the royal side's answers. Dated Tuesday 2 March 1535.
content.remarks: Possibly a minute of the Austro-Venetian arbitration congress at Trent (1533-1535).

content.title: Drafts and letters, 1538-1559
content.persons: Schweikhart (?) von Gundelfingen; Eberhart von Freyberg; Hanns Freiherr zu Wolkenstein
content.description: 82-13, 8 August (?) 1538; 82-7 and 82-8, 20 March 1545, on the publication of a mandate on serfs in the Herrschaft Bregenz; 82-9, 30 March 1545, to a captain; 82-5/82-6, 19 April [15]45, report of the commissioners Schweikhart (?) von Gundelfingen and Eberhart von Freyberg on a diet about aid against the 'Erbfeindt'; 82-11, petition about a fief-holder and the town of Schaffhausen, endorsed 1545; 82-10, report to the emperor, 3 April 155[0 or 6]; 82-4, letter of Hanns Freiherr zu Wolkenstein to royal commissioners, 26 June [15]59.
content.remarks: 82-1 is a 17th-century label; 82-3 a modern parish timetable of Huben (Ötztal).

identification: Three paper scraps: (1) fragment of a German letter by a man serving in a 'Quarde' (Guard), complaining that a promised place was not given and that he waited seven months, with news of the armada (probably army) of a queen 'auss Hungerlan[d](?)' (alt. Engenlan[d]) against 'vnser(s) Khinigl. Armade'; writer, addressee and date lost; (2) Latin scholastic notes on God's omnipresence, 'Conclusio 3.'; (3) a scrap quoting Daniel 12:2
note: On 182_1 the letter was read on the image: the writer reports 'wie es mir biss hero ergangen', that 'der Veldwaibl' and 'den H: Quarde Verwalter' promised him 'einen Plaz', 'aber nit gehalten worden, das ich also [s]ell 7 Monnat wardten müessen', and on the verso mentions debts, service 'in diser Quarde', and news 'Alhie das die Khinigin auss Hungerlan[d](?) Armada ... gegen vnser(s) Khinigl. Armade den 15'. The word check read the country word as 'Hungerlan[d]' (the capital is this hand's H, with four minims before the g), leaving 'Engenlan[d]' only as an alternative; since 'Armada' in 17th-century German usually means an army, no naval event and no date can be inferred, and the month of 'den 15' is lost. On 182_2 the notes read 'Deus ... praesens rebus, quia eas ipse producit ... Deus nec circumscriptive ... loco sed repletive secundum substantiam et operationem' (the doctrine of Aquinas, ST I q. 8), with a marginal addition on 'operationem esse rationem [es]sendi in loco, per virtualem contactum'; the verso has only 'Conclusio 3.'. 182_3 has '...iudice, evigila(bun)t(?) alii in vitam aeternam, alii in opprobrium' (Dan 12:2). A modern pencil note 'aus Einbd. IX/66 v. J. 1641/4[5/6]' gives the host and its date only. Google Books and MDZ searches for the Latin phrases found only the common formula in thesis prints and a doctrinal parallel (Gabriel a S. Vincentio, 1664), and CoMMA gave no lead; the letter has no named party to search by. Partial, chiefly on genre.

content.title: Letter of a man serving in a guard
content.description: The writer complains that a promised place was not given and that he waited seven months, mentions debts and his service 'in diser Quarde', and reports news of the army ('Armada') of a queen 'auss Hungerlan[d]' (?) against 'vnser(s) Khinigl. Armade'. Writer, addressee and date lost.

content.title: Scholastic notes on God's omnipresence
content.description: Deus ... praesens rebus, quia eas ipse producit ... Deus nec circumscriptive ... loco sed repletive secundum substantiam et operationem. Verso: 'Conclusio 3.'
content.remarks: The doctrine of Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q. 8.

content.title: Quotation of Daniel 12:2

identification: Nine paper leaves of German accounts, mostly of the Pfannhausamt (salt-pan office) at Hall in Tirol, 1638-1645: weekly wage and expense lists for weeks 17, 18, 36, 47 and 48 of 1645, an extraordinary-receipts list for the last week of 1638 with a receipt of 17 January 1639 from the 'Pfannhaus Ambts Verwalter' (surname read '[D/V]en[i]s(?) L[e/u]t[z]ij(?)'), a Holzmeisterei list and a widow's pension; mixed with a private interest settlement and older craftsmen's accounts
note: The heading on 2r was read on the image as 'Innamen GOTTES Amen / Die 17. Wochen, A(nn)o 1645', followed by entries for 'Pfannenarbaitern', 'Cleibern' (the daubers who sealed the pans), 'Schreiber' and 'Extra ordinarj Arbaiter'; similar lists are headed weeks 18, 36, 47 and 48 of [16]45. On 6r 'Verzaichnus, was Ich Extra ordinarj Empfanngen, vnnd in die letzte(n) 52 Wochen des 1638 gehörig' includes a receipt from 'Herrn Eitl Hannsen von Sta[c/r]hlburg' for timber and the entry 'Den 17 Jenner des 39 hab Ich vom HH. Hannsen [D/V]en[i]s(?) L[e/u]t[z]ij(?), Pfannhaus Ambts Verwalter' (1496 fl 40 kr); 7r is a 'Provision' for the widow of a former Pfannhausamt officer. The word check confirmed 1645, week 17, 'Pfannhaus Ambts', '-lburg', 1638 and '17 Jenner des 39'; the administrator's surname is two words, the second ending in a written '-ij', which is incompatible with 'Unterrainer'. Schober, Schlossarchiv Fügen (1989), names Hans Unterrainer as Pfannhausamtsverwalter at Hall in 1639 (snippets only), so he is the officer of record that year, but the image does not name him and the identity is not claimed. The 1645 wage lists do not name the office and are assigned to it by their vocabulary and the leaves they travel with; the 4v 'Abraitung mit Herrn Daniel [..]' (interest on 8000, 3000 and 2000 fl) and the columnar craftsmen's accounts on leaf 3 have no visible tie to it, and the 7v/8v interest list rests on the first reading only. The result stays partial because the accountant ('Ich') is unnamed, the leaves are several separate accounts, the office on the 9r endorsement ('Extract a(us) [..]ier(?) Ambts') is unread, and several pages are only partly read.

identification: Horizontal strip of a two-column leaf of a Latin text in short paragraphs with red paraphs, in a small compressed gothic book hand, abraded and stained; only isolated words and point-separated single letters are legible, the genre (natural philosophy or law) is not settled, and the text is not identified
note: Both faces were read on the image at native size, including the upper right column and the left column of 01v, which gave nothing. The legible items are 'mouet aliquod sui', the point-separated letters 'a . c', 'a . d', 'a . g', 'excellentiam' on 01r, and '[paraph] Si quis pet(at)(?)' and 'si habeat' on 01v. The letters can be the terms of a lettered proof in natural philosophy or legal citation sigla, and the words on 01v suit a legal text at least as well, so the genre is open. No phrase of four secure words could be read at the published image quality, so no text was searched or compared; a better image is needed.

content.title: Unidentified scholastic or legal text
content.description: Short paragraphs marked by red paraphs, with point-separated single letters ('a . c', 'a . g'); legible words include 'mouet aliquod sui', 'excellentiam' and 'Si quis'.
content.remarks: Abraded and stained; no connected phrase could be read from the published images. Whether the single letters are proof letters (natural philosophy) or legal citation sigla is not settled.

identification: Four parchment binding strips cut from one early modern Latin document, possibly a chancery or notarial instrument; only one to three words per line survive, and no issuer, party, action, place or date
note: Text was read on the image on face A of strips 2, 3 and 4 only, in one brown-ink hand of the 16th or 17th century; strip 1 and all of face B show no legible ink, also under channel enhancement. Strip 2 gives '[..]?e Hunga[..]' (r or c before e), '[..]m obseruan?[..]', '[..]municatio[..]', '[..]a duntaxa[t]' and '[..]m Aula C[..]'; strip 3 gives '[..]?eom-ensis D[i/u][..]', '[..]?inus No[..]' and '[..]um praenom/praenor[..]'. These words possibly fit a chancery or notarial instrument, but none of them gives a name, act or date, and the place adjective before 'D[i/u]' is not legible. With nothing to anchor a search, the document is not identified.

content.title: Unidentified document
content.remarks: Four binding strips with one to three words per line, in a hand of the 16th or 17th century; possibly a chancery or notarial instrument. No name, place or date survives.

identification: Two small pieces of a two-column manuscript of a Latin logic commentary with dubia, on perfect and imperfect speech, the need for a verb, 'est' as third adjacent, and categorical and hypothetical statements; probably a commentary on Aristotle, Perihermeneias I, chapters 4-5 (book II, chapters 10-11, and Peter of Spain, Tractatus I, are not ruled out); commentary not identified
note: The four faces were read on the image in part, in a minute, heavily abbreviated gothic cursive: 'verbo adiacente alteri verbo', 'quando predicatur 3o adiacens', '[paraph] Item philosophus dicit in ... huius quod', '[paraph] Ad hoc dicendum(?)', 'dicendo(?) homo albus', 'oratio ypothetica ... ligatur', 'cathegorica(?)', 'in interrogatione', 'ad placitum', 'divisio(?) orationum', 'perfectius'. These topics and their order fit Aristotle, Perihermeneias I, chapters 4-5 (17a2-17a22), and two lemmata open with a large initial E(?), as 'Enuntiativa vero' and 'Est autem una prima oratio' would, so the text is probably a commentary with dubia on that passage; book II, chapters 10-11, and the opening of Peter of Spain's Tractatus I were weighed and are less likely but not ruled out, and no lemma was read securely. The wording was not found by text search in Thomas Aquinas's commentary, nor by Google Books, Internet Archive, Corpus Corporum and CoMMA searches (CoMMA top hit below the shuffled-query null); the 13th-century commentaries with dubia that are unprinted or not searchable were not tested.

content.title: Logic commentary with dubia, probably on Aristotle, Perihermeneias I, chapters 4-5
content.description: On perfect and imperfect speech ('homo albus', 'in interrogatione'), the need for a verb, 'est' predicated as third adjacent, and categorical and hypothetical statements ('oratio ypothetica ... ligatur'). Dubia are introduced by 'Item' and answered 'Ad hoc dicendum(?)'.
content.remarks: The topics and their order fit Perihermeneias I, 4-5 (17a2-17a22), and two lemmata open with a large initial E(?); Perihermeneias II, 10-11, and Peter of Spain, Tractatus I, are not ruled out. The left piece is photographed upside down on both images. The commentary is not identified.

identification: Pieces 104_2 and 104_3: Sermones de tempore printed among Bonaventure's works (Peltier ed., Opera omnia XIII, 1868), attributed to Conrad of Saxony (Holtnicker): 104_2, an outer-bifolium strip, has Feria II Pentecostes sermons II-III (Peltier pp. 308-310) and the 'De Lazaro' part of Dominica II post Pentecosten sermon II (p. 333), with one column from a sermon Peltier does not print; 104_3 has the opening of that Dominica II sermon (pp. 332b-333a); pieces 104_4, 104_5 and 104_6 are unidentified; 104_1 is a ruled blank leaf with illegible offset
note: Several columns of 104_2 and the line beginnings of 104_3 run with Peltier XIII on the page images of pp. 309 and 332 (e.g. 'Si replete fuerint nubes ymbre(m) ... Nubes iste ap(osto)li (et) doctores', p. 309b); the attribution to Conrad of Saxony rests on Schneyer's cross-reference and the rubrics of Klosterneuburg CCl 451, both seen in snippets or catalogue OCR only. Pieces 104_4-6 have the same line spacing and script as 104_2-3 and carry one series of medieval item numbers ('c94', 'ccxx', 'ccxxi' under a 'C'), but the words read on them ('insipientes', 'commendare', 'rationis prestan-' on 104_4) are not in Peltier XIII or XIV on cluster and edit-tolerant searches of the OCR, and Corpus Corporum and CoMMA gave no lead. The column of 104_2 that Peltier does not print ('venenata', 'ad vulnerandum', 'Sagitta' twice) may be the sermon 'Mitte Lazarum ... Misera lingua inflammabitur' listed by Schneyer for the preceding Sunday; no text of it was available, and the images of Klosterneuburg CCl 451 could not be consulted because manuscripta.at was unavailable. With three text-bearing pieces unmatched the record stays partial.

fragmentarium.title: Sermones de tempore

content.title: Sermones de tempore printed among the works of Bonaventure, attributed to Conrad of Saxony (Holtnicker)
content.description: 104_2: Feria II Pentecostes, sermons II-III, and the 'De Lazaro' part of Dominica II post Pentecosten, sermon II, with one column from a sermon not printed by Peltier. 104_3: opening of the same Dominica II sermon.
content.remarks: Schneyer refers these sermons to Conradus Holtnicker; Klosterneuburg, CCl 451 has the rubrics 'Chunradini' and 'fratris Chunradini' for them.

content.title: Unidentified text, probably sermons
content.description: Small strips with line beginnings and ends in the same script and line spacing as 104_2 and 104_3, with scriptural citations (Gen., Luc.) and the medieval item numbers 'c94', 'ccxx' and 'ccxxi'.
content.remarks: Not found in Peltier, Opera omnia XIII-XIV. 104_1 is a ruled blank leaf with mirror-image offset of a cursive hand.

identification: Ps.-Siricius, letter to Theodorus of Córdoba 'Litteris a tua fraternitate directis' (long form), preceded by the end of the expanded Ps.-Gregory 'Statuimus secundum priorem diffinitionem'
note: The leaf carries the inscription 'fratri Theodoro Cordubensi episcopo', the incipit with a red initial, and the body of the forged Ps.-Siricius letter on giving tithes and altar offerings to monks, into its long ending ('decernimus inconuulsa ... ubi nichil'); an independent reader collated canvas 1 lines 9-18 with the page image of Vat. lat. 1361 fol. 245va-b (Collection in 13 Books 13.42), and a research reader compared the earlier part with Paxton's edition from Leipzig 276 (snippets). The six lines before the inscription match the end of the expanded Ps.-Gregory 'Statuimus' that Pfurtscheller (1972) printed from Stams Cod. 17 fol. I'r, seen in Google Books snippets only; the coordinator read canvas 0 lines 5-7 on the image. Differences: 'decime conueniunt' without 'dari', 'fuerunt' for 'fuerint', and a probable omission of 'Horum sustentationem ... obtinebis'. The collection containing the two texts is not named, and the copy is not dated.

identification: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae IIIa, table of questions and articles, qq. 33-37 and 40-45
note: Red question headings with numbers run unbroken through IIIa qq. 33-37 (canvas 1, 01v) and qq. 40-45 (canvas 0, 01r), in the wording of the standard table of the Summa as printed in the 1879 Paris and Bar-le-Duc index, not that of the Leonine question prologues; the abraded brown lines give the articles, legibly for qq. 33, 34, 35, 36 and 40, and name article contents (q. 35 a. 7 'Bethleem') rather than copying the prologues. A research reader compared headings and article lines with the Leonine text (Corpus Thomisticum transcription); an independent reader compared the q. 35 article lines and the q. 37 heading with page images of the 1879 index; the coordinator read the canvas 0 headings on the image. The q. 37 heading reads 'cisione pueri(?) legalibus ihu obseruatis', near the index's 'De legalibus circa puerum Jesum observantiis'. Whether the table stood alone or was bound with a copy of the third part, and the date of the copy, are not established.

identification: Judgment of Hanns Rott, judge in a fief case, for the procurator of Stams abbey: Balthasar Mitterhofer's holding (garden or Platz) at Nauders declared fallen back to the abbey; 16th century, date not established
note: Regest read on the image (fol. 2r, 1v, 1r): Hanns Rott as Lehenrichter, with the fellow vassals, declares Mitterhofer's tenancy of a plot before his house at Nauders forfeited to the abbot and convent of Stams (procurator Peter N(?)üben) and seals with his pendant seal. The opening leaves are lost and the date is not established (it may be in an unread faded block on fol. 2v). The same plot and tenant appear in the regest of Stams Urk. L_LXXIX_2, Abbot Pelagius's grant to Mitterhofer of 1534, compared by a research reader on monasterium.net (regest only; a related act, not a record of this judgment); the judgment is probably later than that grant, an inference not a reading. A modern pencil note on canvas 0, '1534 2[6/8] Juni', has an unknown relation to the act and was not used. Word crops for the names were read blind by two readers and adjudicated; the procurator's surname stays uncertain.
