identification: Tyrolean German deed of sale ('Kauffbrief') on parchment, second half of the sixteenth century by the script, 'nach dem gemainen Tirolischen Lanndtsprauch', possibly drawn up at Partschins near Meran (a single reader's reading, not confirmed by a blind reader): buyer 'Anndreen(?) Kolmans', a curator acting as attorney for one party, witnesses 'All drey zu p[ar]tschins Sess[haft]' and 'Alexannder Rodt schreiber daselbs'; 17 November, year lost; vendor and object not securely read; later the cover of a Stams Oberkelleramt register
note: The text face (image 01v) names the buyer 'Anndreen(?) Kolmans, als Kauffers', a 'volmechtiger Churator vnnd gewalthaber', and witnesses 'Petter H[..]nz(?) Pre[..]l[..]ner(?), All drey zu p[ar]tschins Sess[haft], vnd Alexannder Rodt schrei[ber] daselbs', so the deed was possibly drawn up at Partschins near Meran (these words were read by one reader only; a blind reader of the same crops did not confirm 'Partschins' or 'Rodt' and read the buyer's surname '[K/R]ol[.]man'); the property clause has 'Recht Jm Tablannd[..](?)'. It is dated 'Beschehen am Sibenze[h]enden tag Monats Nouembris, Nach Christi Jhesu vnnsers Erlösers', and the year runs onto the right turn-in under the photographer's weight. The display line may begin '[I]ch(?) Hanns(?) Pau[..](?)' and the endorsement on the back reads 'Kauffbrief vmb den paung[art..](?)', perhaps an orchard, but vendor and object are not securely read. No charter in the Stams fonds on monasterium.net names Kolman, Rodt or Partschins (search and a word search of the 1525-1612 regests), so no outside record of the act is known.

content.title: Deed of sale
content.description: Sale 'nach dem gemainen Tirolischen Lanndtsprauch' to the buyer Anndreen (?) Kolman, with a curator acting as attorney for one party; witnesses 'All drey zu p[ar]tschins Sess[haft]' and Alexander Rodt, scribe there, so possibly drawn up at Partschins near Meran (not confirmed by a blind reading). Dated 17 November, year lost. Vendor and object not securely read.
content.remarks: Endorsement on the back: 'Kauffbrief vmb den paung[art..] (?)'. The year is hidden on the right turn-in.

identification: Two parchment binding-waste leaves of a German sixteenth-century prose document in fast chancery cursive, apparently a letter, report or petition to a lord ('E(uer) G(naden)'), opening with a display word '[..](e/a)rlannder.'; issuer, addressee, matter and date not read
note: Face B (canvas 1, leaves 2v and 1v) carries the legible text, read on the image: the display word '[..](e/a)rlannder.' (letter before r e or a, followed by a point) and 'auf dem' followed by a looped capital, R or L, unresolved; then scattered words such as 'vnd bewilligung', '[ab]schrifftlichen zuegestelt', 'aufs fleissigist', '[..]tagen vnd bezallen', 'die handlungen', 'von Doctorn', 'Ich abgemelten' and 'E(uer) G(naden)(?)'. The word check confirmed the heading only with that caveat, left the capital after 'auf dem' open, and gave no reading for a third word, so nothing rests on it. The right halves of both pages are faded beyond reading, and face A is show-through apart from a later pen trial ('[..] Rats(?) vom yezt(?) Kaiß(?) kauff[..]'). A '1567(?)' seen by the first reader on a torn corner was not confirmed. Whether the heading is a word such as '[Nid]erlannder' or '[Ob]erlannder' and the phrase a 'Reichstag' or 'Landtag' is a lead only; Google Books searches for '"Niderlannder" "auf dem Reichstag" beschwerden bewilligung' and 'abschrifftlichen zuegestelt' gave no hits, and no connected span of more than three or four secure words exists for further searching. No issuer, addressee, action or date can be read; multispectral or UV imaging, or reading at the object under raking light, would be needed.

identification: Narrow vertical strip with the cut-off middles of about 12-14 lines of a very faded late-medieval cursive on one face; language and genre not established
note: Face A carries the middles of about 12-14 lines, cut at both edges, in the upper two thirds of the strip. Blue-channel enhanced crops give only letter shapes: a possible 'It(em)?' at a line start, 'gene(?)', 'p(re)?', a word-end 'bus' and a word beginning 'Ca[..]', none secure. Whether the text is Latin or German is not settled, and the impression of accounts or a register rests only on the documentary look and the possible 'Item'. Face B has no writing and shows fine striations that look like paper laid lines, although the catalogue says parchment; the material should be checked on the original. No sequence of words was readable, so nothing was searched; multispectral or UV imaging of face A is the only way forward.

identification: Unidentified Latin text in a large Gothic book hand with two-line red initials and a red rubric ending 'Iohannem' (small piece cut into four strips, no staves)
note: One face keeps line beginnings with two-line red initials: 'Quo..', 'lux' or 'iux..', 'immun..' or 'in mun..', 'Et ideo' and 'Ego su[m]'. The other keeps line ends, among them the red rubric '[..] Iohem' (Iohannem). A research reader read '..t inuic[em]' and 'manet in m[e]' with John 15 in mind, suggesting Mass lessons or chants from John 15, but a blind reader of the same crops did not confirm either word (it read '[..]manıs(?) tuı[.]' and unresolved minims), so no text is proposed. A modern pencil shelfmark note on the piece was not used.

content.title: Unidentified text
content.description: Four cut strips of one piece in a large Gothic book hand without staves. Line beginnings on one face (Quo.., Et ideo, Ego su[m], with two-line red initials), line ends on the other (red rubric ending Iohannem).
content.remarks: Not identified; a suggested link with John 15 rests on two words not confirmed by a blind reading.

identification: Vertical parchment strip from a German deed or grant in a fifteenth-century (or c. 1500) cursive, one or two words from each of about 32 lines ('Erb', 'Recht(?) od[er]', '[v]erlihen(?)', 'Allso', a princely title 'Durchl[e]ucht[..](?)'); no issuer, party, object, place or date survives
note: The strip (canvas 0) keeps a narrow vertical slice near one edge of a single-column German document; every line was reread on the image, giving deed vocabulary such as '[..]d Jr E[..]', '[..]y Erb', 'Allso' with an enlarged initial, '[..]Recht(?) od[er]', '[..]willigkait(?)', 'so mügen(?)' and '[..]erlihen(?)', which suggests a grant or conveyance to heirs. The word check corrected the last line from 'Durstanta' or 'Deutschen' to '[..]y Durchl[e]ucht[..](?)', a form of 'Durchleuchtig', the style of a prince, so a prince was named or addressed, but who is lost. The back has no medieval writing; a modern pencil host note, confirmed by the word check, reads 'aus P. Kerii Germani[a] / Inferior, Amsterdam 1682', with the third digit more likely 8 than 3, which would make the host a copy of Petrus Kaerius, Germania inferior; this records the reported host volume, not when the strip was bound into it, and the edition was not verified. With no party, place or date, no search was run and no regest is possible.

identification: German deed of 1575, probably a draft: abbot Johannes, 'Regierennder Prelat' of a house whose name is torn away (possibly Stams under abbot Johann Kölbel, if the Weingarten estate had passed to Stams by then; Weingarten's own abbot in 1575 was also a Johannes), grants in heritable tenure the 'Marätsch(?) hof', probably the Maratschhof at the old toll in Mitterplars (Töll, parish of Algund), a former Weingarten farm, with buildings, fields and vineyards, to a tenant whose name is lost and his heirs, against yearly dues including half the wine, saving the rights of the lordship of Schloss Tirol; on the other face the later cover title of an account book (158x)
note: The deed on 194v opens 'Wir Johannes Abbt vnnd Regierennder Prelat des Wirdigen Go[...]' and is dated in words 1575; the house name and the tenant's name are lost with the cut top-right corner. The boundary clause names the granted farm as 'disen Marätsch(?) hof' (first reading 'Grätsch?'; the M was read with the repertory in view and a blind reader did not confirm it, though the initial matches the M of 'Mittag' in the next line, and the same farm name with a Wonhofer neighbour stands in the earlier reading of another Stams fragment, F-0dnc) and its neighbours Schaittenhof, Wiltenhof, ober Flatten, '[W/M]onhofers ackher' and a field 'Zu Partschinß gehörig': these names correspond, as spelling equations, to the farms of the Maratschhof at the old toll in Mitterplars (Töll, parish of Algund), which Tarneller's farm-name repertory (Archiv für österreichische Geschichte 100, 1910, pp. 122-124, read as snippets) records as serving Weingarten abbey in 1439 and under Stams as landlord in 1633, beside the farms Wonhof, Wild and Platt. Line 3 refers to the custom and right 'der Ambte Zu Lanan(?), So von dem Würdigen Gotzhaus Weing[...]', which fits Weingarten's estate administered from Lana, so the issuer is possibly abbot Johann Kölbel of Stams (1567-1590), on the condition, not checked on a record, that the Weingarten estate had passed to Stams by 1575 (Weingarten's own abbot in 1575 was also a Johannes; no exchange was found in a keyword search of the Stams regests 1545-1549); the house name itself is not read, and St Mang in Füssen, landlord of the farm by 1780, is unlikely for 1575 but not excluded. Outside records name Clauß Nieberl 'genant Marätscher' in 1571 and Sigmund Jäger 'genannt Marätscher' in 1584 (Stiftsarchiv Wilten, Urkunden 190 X 09), but neither is read on the leaf, and no record of the 1575 act was found (monasterium.net Stams regests 1572-1580 read in full; Lebersorg's Stams chronicle p. 541, which mentions the Maratschhof, not seen), so the result stays partial.

fragmentarium.title: Grant of a farm, probably the Maratschhof at Mitterplars (Algund)

content.title: Grant of a farm, probably the Maratschhof, by abbot Johannes, 1575
content.description: Johannes, abbot and 'Regierennder Prelat' of a house whose name is lost, possibly Stams, grants in heritable tenure the 'Marätsch(?) hof' (probably the Maratschhof at the old toll in Mitterplars, parish of Algund) with buildings, fields and vineyards to a tenant and his heirs, against yearly dues including half the wine, saving the rights of the lordship of Schloss Tirol, and seals with the abbey seal. 1575, no day or month.
content.remarks: Probably a draft. The Maratschhof served Weingarten abbey in the fifteenth century and had Stams as landlord in 1633 (Tarneller); the issuer is possibly abbot Johann Kölbel of Stams (1567-1590), if the estate had passed to Stams by 1575. Another Stams fragment, F-0dnc, also names the Maratschhof. The tenant's name is lost.

identification: Torn paper scraps on a tissue mount from an early modern German account or list in Kurrent (probably seventeenth or eighteenth century), entries running out in filler rules to sums in fl and kr; with two blank scalloped paper ovals; no names, dates or headings
note: About ten scraps on a grey tissue mount (canvases 0 and 1) were read on the image in autocontrast crops: '[..]r dahin', 'Vnnd zwayen(?) traidt' (Kurrent g and y are alike, so 'zwagen' is possible; 'zwayen traidt' would be a payment in grain), '36 fl(?)' with '[.]6 kr(?)', '[..]ichsgelt(?) ... 3 kr(?)', '1008(?)' and '[..] Pfenni(n)gen(?)'. Filler rules run to an amount column, which with the fl and kr units marks the scraps as accounts or a list of dues. Two loose scalloped ovals above the mount show only grime and may be decorative seal covers, which was not tested. No name, place, date or connected phrase survives that any source could index, so no search was run. Comparison of the hand and units with dated Stams account books might date it.

identification: Fourteen paper binding-waste slips from early modern letters (probably sixteenth century), in Latin humanist cursive and German Kurrent, often on the two faces of one slip; writer, addressee, place and date lost
note: Read on the image of slip 1v is the close of a Latin private letter: '[..] non paruisse . Vale, et dic Iohani, quia hact(enu)s(?) [..]ur(?) me quam primum et uilissime libros illius uenundaturum nisi intra duodecim dies satisfe[cerit]', a threat to sell one Johannes's books unless he pays within twelve days. Its German back (1a) gives letter news: 'Der rat(?) hat etlichen den lanzknechten den lon gedoplt(?) . Nicolau[s] hat den gartten ... verkauft', and the Landsknecht wording points to the sixteenth century. Slips 6a, 8a and 13a carry further Latin in a like hand ('famulus' on 6a and 13a, 'Petrum', 'fortem(?) fustibus', 'partem curie'); the other slips were checked only on the overviews. Phrase searches in Google Books, the Internet Archive and Corpus Corporum ('libros illius venundaturum', 'intra duodecim dies satisfecerit', 'dic Iohanni quia hactenus', 'fuit sponsa parens') found no printed source, and the CoMMA batch search gave no lead. No name of writer or addressee, no place and no date survive, so no regest is possible; matching hands across other Stams binding waste from the same host is the remaining route.

identification: Paper strip from a bifolium with four framed single-column pages of very rapid Latin cursive (late fifteenth or sixteenth century), apparently documentary or legal prose from a register, copybook or draft book; issuer, addressee, action and date not established
note: The strip crosses a folded sheet and keeps about 14 lines from each of four framed pages; there is no seal, signature, endorsement or address. The hand uses virgules as punctuation; the secure words are 'd(omi)ni honorab(i)l(i)s', 'atq(ue)', 'Et aliud', 'sibi' and 'alios' on 94r and 'quib(us)d(am) mo(n)ast(er)iis', probably followed by 'in perpetuum', on 94v. A word on 94r that begins at an ink blot was not confirmed as a month name, uncertain readings such as 'inquit?' and 'vetula?' leave a sermon or exemplum text possible, and the double-f forms are not followed by a title or law, so civil-law citations are not shown. Phrase searches (Corpus Corporum, Google Books, Internet Archive, MDZ) found nothing, and no party, place or act could be read; the right block of 94v is covered by rust spotting.

content.title: Unidentified text, apparently documentary or legal prose
content.description: Strip across a bifolium with about 14 lines from each of four framed pages in a rapid cursive with virgules. Legible words include domini honorabilis, atque, Et aliud, sibi, alios, quibusdam monasteriis.

identification: Leaves 165/2-1 to 4, 21 and 29 to 33, and probably 13-14: one copy of the Council of Basel's official Acta of the first session, 14 December 1431 (protonotaries' preamble 'Censetur utique dignum', acts of 7 and 14 December 1431, and the decree on those who hinder people coming to the council, with the Council of Constance's constitution 'Iusticiam et equitatem' of 6 July 1415 inserted in full), matching Mansi XXIX cols. 3-5 and 15-19; the other leaves: papers of a suit at Basel in 1434 probably over defamations and injuries before Albert Varrentrapp, decretorum doctor, cantor of Liège, judge-commissary deputed by the council, between Nicolaus Volrat, abbreviator of apostolic letters and dean of St John in Haug (Würzburg), and Wilhelm (Guillelmus) de Grumpach, a canon in the diocese of Würzburg; and acts of a second Basel suit of October-November 1438
note: Paper leaves from the binding of Stams MS 59, holding three separate parts. The Acta copy has the preamble and the acts of 7 and 14 December 1431 on leaves 1-4 (2r agrees line by line with Mansi XXIX cols. 4-5), then on 2v the heading 'Sequuntur decreta lecta In prima sessione' and on 1r the close of the decree on those who hinder people coming to the council, 'locum habere declarat et decernit iuxta ipsius que talis est seriem et tenorem', followed by the inserted Constance constitution 'Sacrosancta generalis Sinodus Constanciensis ... Iusticiam et equitatem exerceri non dubitatur', whose faces follow in the printed order over leaves 33, 21, 31, 32, 30 and 29, with about 25 words (five to seven lines) lost at each of the six changes of face measured, as on leaves trimmed at the head, to its dating clause on 29r ('Datum Constancie se[..] [no]nas Julii ... Sigismundi Roma[norum] ac vngarie etc. Regis ... Hungarie vero vi[cesimo] nono'); 1r, 21v, 32v, 29v and 29r agree with the page images of Mansi XXIX cols. 15-19 apart from small variants ('festiuis' and 'villas castra' on 29v; probably 'papali' for 'pontificali' on 31v-32r), the year word on 29r is only partly legible, and several faces were placed from reduced images and leaves 13-14 only probably, from the first reading. In the 1434 suit the image gives 'Mandat magister Albertus Varrentrapp decretorum doctor Cantor Leodien(sis) iudex et commissarius' (27r), 'Nicholaum Volrat litterarum apostolicarum abbreviatorem decanum ecclesie sancti Johannis in Haugis extra muros Herbi[polensis]' and the object 'de et super nonnullis diffa[macio]nibus Iniuriis rebusque aliis' (7r, 5r), with the year 1434, the month June (the day 25 only on a modern red slip) and 3 August 1434 (5r). Leaves 34-42 hold acts of a second suit at Basel dated 3 and 5 November 1438, before a bishop sitting for the council's court of causes and concerning Otto Grauer(?), a perpetual vicar in the diocese of Mainz, and are only partly read. No record of either suit was found by text search in Concilium Basiliense II, III, IV and VII, so the record stays partial.

identification: Jean de Blanot (Johannes de Blanasco), Libellus super titulo Institutionum de actionibus: end of the chapter on the actio negotiorum gestorum and the secundum caput of the actio utilis negotiorum gestorum (strip 1); actio tutelae and contraria actio tutelae (strips 3 and 2)
note: On strip 1, ten line ends of face 1v agree in sequence with Blanot's commentary in the 1568 print, fol. 276r-v ('quando quis sponte administrat ... non sponte administrat ... necessitatis suspicione habebit locum negotiorum ... l. atqui natura § si libero'). Face 1r has the following chapter's 'negotii in quo male se habuerit ... formatur libellus' with the red rubric 'Libellus'. Two research readers compared these lines with page images of the print, and the coordinator read 1v lines 4-7 before seeing the source. Strips 3 (3v) and 2 (2v col. b) are placed in the same work at fol. 277v and 278r by a run of matching words on stained surfaces, without a full collation. The only noted difference is word order on 1v line 9 ('non tamen est necessitas' against 'non tamen necessitas est'). No modern edition was compared, and the rectos of strips 2 and 3 are unread.

identification: Two small scraps with parts of about 13 lines each of a German legal or administrative text in a seventeenth-century Kurrent hand ('oder ausserha[lb]', 'rechten', '[e]xecution(?)', '[..]schulden(?) ist', 'wie lang', 'od(er) andere(?) sachen'); no issuer, party, place or date
note: Only the second face (canvas 1) shows writing: the right scrap (22-1v) keeps line beginnings and the left scrap (22-2v) line ends, both abraded; the other face shows no letters. Read on the image on 22-1v are 'oder ausserha[lb(?)]', '[..]rechten', '[e]xecution(?) Kauff(?)[..]', '[..]schulden(?) ist', 'Zusammen(?)', 'wie lang' and '[..]nnuß(?) od(er) andere(?) sachen'; 22-2v gives only scattered German word ends. The word check found that the first word of line 4, earlier taken as 'Kauffschilling' (purchase price), begins with a P to all three readers and reads only 'Pa[..]f/ſ[..](?)', so 'Kauffschilling' is a conjecture that would need a K, and the text cannot be said to concern a purchase price. The vocabulary of execution and debts suggests a legal or administrative text, perhaps a copy from a printed ordinance, but the line fragments are too short and uncertain to search. Whether the two scraps come from the same page is not decidable. No search was run and no regest is possible.

identification: Piece 152-2: Codex Iustinianus, 8.13.27 pr.-1 (2r, line beginnings) and 8.14.2 (end), 8.14.3 (complete) and the opening of 8.14.4 (2v), numbering of Krueger's edition, p. 341; small Gothic textualis. Pieces 152-3, -4 and -5 are in a different, later hand with red underlining and are not identified; the long strip 152-1 is not placed and its relation to 152-2 is open
note: A research reader and an independent checker, the checker reading the piece before opening the edition, compared piece 152-2 with Krueger's edition on the page image: one face has six line beginnings in order from C. 8.13.27 pr.-1, the other the end of C. 8.14.2, a largely illegible heading line, C. 8.14.3 in six consecutive full lines to 'nulli [prudentium] placuit', then 'Imp.' and probably 'Satis notum est' (8.14.4); about 25 words agree in order. It is the Codex text itself (constitutions with inscriptions, not a Summa or apparatus); gloss can be neither shown nor excluded on the narrow surviving margin. Three small words in 8.14.3 are faded, one ('ex ipis' or 'et ipsi') left open, and 8.14.2 ends 'exprimitur'. Pieces 152-3, 152-4 and 152-5 are in a larger, later hand and are not identified; the strip 152-1, in a small textualis compatible with 152-2, is not placed and a comparison with C. 8.13.20-8.18.3 found no match. The catalogue's dimensions are those of the strip 152-1; date and origin are not claimed.

identification: Noted Mass book (gradual or noted missal), Good Friday, Adoration of the Cross: Improperia verse Quid ultra debui ... Ego quidem plantavi te vineam meam speciosissimam (Cantus 008453); antiphon Ecce lignum crucis ... venite adoremus (Cantus 002522) with verse Beati [immaculati]
note: Two paper scraps of one leaf with Hufnagel notation on red staves. One face reads '[d]e bui face re ti[bi] / [E]go(?) quide(m) planta ui te uine[am] [m]eā spe c[iosissimam]', with the line running across both scraps; the other reads '[mu]ndi pepen[dit] ... a do re mus | Beati'. A research reader matched every line to the Cantus Index standard texts. An independent research reader reread the weakest lines on the images and compared the words with the Graduale Romanum 1908, pp. 182-183, and the verse Beati immaculati with Martène's printed ordo, on page images: no difference in the surviving letters. 'Ego' is not secure; use, date and leaf order (the two printed sources disagree on the order of the chants) are not determined.

identification: Bundle of at least nine German paper receipts, chancery notes and account strips of the Habsburg administration of Tyrol and Further Austria, sixteenth century to 1608: receipt of Jacob S[...]berg, Zeugwart, for 12 fl. (Freitag(?) [day unread] July, year unread; a modern note proposes 2 July 1508); receipt of Leonhart [...], Landvogtschreiber zu Burgau, for 14 fl.; receipt of a salaried officer, December 1582, dorsal 'zu Holzhaim(e)'; receipt of Thomas [Re]ntz, Landammann(?) of the Markgrafschaft Burgau, for 200 fl., under Archduke Ferdinand; a note of 26 July [..]4 of the Landvogt and 'Räth zu obern Ellsäß' (presumably the government at Ensisheim); a 1608 Fiat and related notes
note: Frg. 110 holds strips of at least nine separate documents, not one text. D1, a receipt, reads 'Ich Jacob S[...]berg Ro(mi)sch(?) kay(?) m(aies)t zeugwartter bekenn' for 'Zwelff gulden' of service money under his Bestellbrief; its dating clause gives 'geben ist F[reitag?] ... monats Julij Anno d(omi)ni' followed by year words that the word check found unreadable, so the year and the day are not read: the day 2 and the year 1508 come only from the modern pencil note 'Freitag 2. July 1508', and the weekday cannot decide the year because the day is not on the leaf. The title words stay queried and are not used for dating; 'Rei[nisch]' after the sum and the red-pencil 'den' in the gap of the surname are modern restorations on the repair strip, not readings. D2 is read as 'Ich Leonhart [...] Landtvogtschreiber zur Burg[au](?)', paid 'vierzehen gulden besold[ung]' by the Kay. Mt.'s officer in the Markgrafschaft Burgau, date lost; D3 ends 'den 2[.] Decembris Ao 8[.]' with the year 1582 resting on the dorsal '.82.', which also reads 'zu Holzhaime'. D4 reads 'Ich Thoma[s] ... [Re]ntz F. Dt. Ertzhertzog Ferdinan[ds] ... [l]andtaman(?) der Marggra[fschaft]' and 'zwaihundert guldin', which fits Ferdinand II as lord of Burgau (1564-1595); a Thomas Rentz, Landammann of Burgau, is attested c. 1580 in a Reichskammergericht inventory (snippet), which corroborates the person, not this receipt. D5 is a chancery note of 26 July [..]4 subscribed by the Landvogt, Regenten 'vnnd Räth zu obern Ellsäß', recording 200 fl. paid for future equipment; the decade is lost in the hinge. D6 is a 'Fiat für Herrn Camerer' dated 'Anno 1608', with short protocol notes and account strips of the same period. No outside record of any of these acts was found; the result is partial because names, dates and the D1 year are lost in hinge gaps or under the repair strip and most pieces give only part of their regest.

identification: Three unrelated parchment scraps: (A, item 3) a printed breviary, probably of the use of Brixen, third Sunday of Advent and the following week (Benedictus antiphon Johannes autem, Terce chapter Nolite ante tempus iudicare; antiphons Elevare elevare, Ponam in Sion, Ponent domino; invitatory Surgite vigilemus), text as in the Breviarium Brixinense of Venice 1516 but another edition, not found; (B) a manuscript computus, possibly in verse, with red rubrics, unplaced; (C) an unread strip
note: Scrap A is printed in red and black in two columns, in a rotunda type of about 62 mm to 20 lines. Its recto has the end of the antiphon '[an alium] expectam(us)', a red rubric and the chapter '[N]olite a[nte tempus iudicare] quoad[usque ...] ⁊ illumina[bit ... tene]brarum ⁊ m[anifestabit]'; its verso has '[consur]ge iherusale(m) ... [t]ui captiua fi[lia]', red '[Feria qu]arta an.' 'Po[nam ...] ⁊ in iherusa[lem ... a]lleluia', red 'an.' '[...] ⁊ laude(m) ei(us) ... quia ecce' and, in the next column, 'Sur[gite vigile]mus'. Text, rubric wording and order agree in both columns of both faces with the Brixen breviary printed at Venice in 1516 (Munich, BSB, Liturg. 101, scans 243-244, compared on the page), but spellings and line breaks differ, so the scrap is probably from another edition of that breviary; Ratdolt's of 1489 has a type of this size and could not be compared, and breviaries of neighbouring dioceses were not compared. Scrap B has red rubrics ('[q]ui nesciunt algorismum', '[...]nibus et officio xii mensium') and lines marked by red paraphs with marginal notes, its black text abraded; scrap C was not read.

identification: Scraps of an Office book with lessons and responsories: lessons from the homily Surdus ille et mutus on Mark 7:31-37 under the rubric 'Omelia v. b[...]' (Bede, PL 94, 290 D and 291 B-C) and from the preceding Luke 18:12 homily (PL 94, 290 B; the sentence is Gregory's, taken over by Bede), with the Job responsory Numquid Dominus supplantat iudicium (Cantus 007244) and probably Versa est in luctum (Cantus 007846)
note: After a red S and the rubric 'Omelia . v . b[...]' the 01r scrap reads '[S]urdus ille et', the incipit of the homily on Mark 7:31-37 printed among Bede's homilies in PL 94 (290 D); three line beginnings read with the source as 'custodia(m) / q(uo)d co(n)t(r)a [h]ostiu(m) insid[ias] / tota' stand at the expected intervals in the Luke 18 homily printed just before it (290 B), and the back of those scraps has 'seorsu(m)' and '[au]riculas' at line ends where the Mark homily predicts them (291 B-C); compared on page images of PL 94. The image-only first reading has compatible letter groups there ('custodia', 'q(uo)d' ... osti(?) ... fid[...]', 'tota(?)', 'uersu(m)(?)', '[.]rticulas'); the fuller wording is a reconstruction made with the source. The small-script scrap has the Job responsory Numquid Dominus (Cantus 007244) on 01v; the other face is probably Versa est in luctum (Cantus 007846), read with the text in view and not confirmed by a blind reader. The Luke sentence is Gregory's, taken over by Bede, so the three part-lines cannot exclude Gregory's text; the faded red letters on 01v are the recto rubric showing through; the responsory scrap is not in its original position, so the same book is likely but the same leaf is not shown; faint strokes above the chant lines may be staffless neumes, and the kind of book, its use and date are not established.

identification: Two strips of one German deed of sale in a sixteenth-century Kurrent hand: [sellers lost], a couple, with the knowledge and consent of the honourable and spiritual lord Hannsen p(?)ay(r?), Capp[..], appointed Castner zu [S/C]and[..]..rg(?), sell ('hingeben vnnd verkaufft') to Thoman(?) Ha[..]s(?) and his wife Dorothea a share ('d(r)ey(?) vi[er]ta[y]ll(?)') of a right 'Ba[..]' in a holding at '[..]ets(?)' held of the 'Herrschafft zur [S/C]and[..]'; the names Payr, Freundsberg and St. Petersberg, the Baurecht, the three-quarter share and Rietz are supplied by a modern typed slip and pencil notes, not read on the strips; date lost
note: The written face (canvas 0) carries two non-contiguous strips of about four long lines each; read on the image are the acknowledgement 'Bekhennen baide vnuerschidenlichen mit disem offnen Brief fur vnns vnnd all vnnsre baider Erben', the consent of 'des Ersamen vnnd geistlichen Herren Hannsen p(?)ay(r?) Capp[..]', 'verordneter [..]waltiger Castner zu [S/C]and[..]', the sale clause 'hingeben vnnd verkaufft', the buyers 'Thoman(?) Ha[..]s(?)' and 'Dorothea seiner hausfrawen', and '[..]ets(?) obgemelt gelegen das von der Herrschafft zur [S/C]and[..]'. The word check reduced the surname after Hannsen to 'p(?)ay(r?)' (only 'a y' secure), found the place after 'von' in line U3 illegible, saw only 'zu', 'and' and a final '-rg' in the Castner's seat, with all three blind readers seeing an initial C rather than S, cut the right sold to 'Ba[..]', left the share as traces only, corrected 'zu' to 'zur' before the lordship, and reduced the buyer's surname to 'Ha[..]s(?)'. The readings 'Payr', 'Capp[lan]', 'Frewnsperg', 'Sandpetersperg', 'Bawrecht drey viertayll', 'Riets' and 'Valtein' are therefore not read on the leaf and come from the modern typed transcription slip and pencil notes on the back, which are the same object, not an independent record. The regest as Hanns Payr, Kastner of St. Petersberg for the Freundsberg family, consenting to a sale of three quarters of a Baurecht at Rietz, and the date bound 1407-1586 (the Freundsberg tenure of Petersberg, Fornwagner 1992, snippet only), all rest on that slip; the modern pencil dates '1529?' and red '1491?' are unchecked notes. The sellers' names, the price and the dating clause are lost. Searches in Google Books, the Imst Gemeindearchive inventory and monasterium.net for Hans Payr as Kastner or chaplain, Kastner of Petersberg and Rietz Baurecht found no matching act. It stays partial at low confidence because the action (a sale) is read but the consenting official, the object and the lordship rest chiefly on the modern slip.

identification: Two separate German deeds (items 128_1 and 128_2) reused as binding wrappers (host pencilled 'aus VIII E 7'), almost entirely abraded, action and principal parties unread: document 2 is dated in the 33rd year of an unread century ('Drey vnnd d[..]ſten Jaren(?)'), Monday before St Thomas 1533 (15 Dec 1533) only from a modern pencil note, and names a '[Ger]ichtſchreiber(?) zu Ca/La..z(?)' and witnesses; document 1 has a sealing clause naming the 'Herrschafft Tirol', date lost
note: The text faces are 128_1v and 128_2v, each with about 26-30 long lines in a German Kurrent that looks sixteenth-century; only the last four to six lines of each were read on the image, and the outer faces show ruled bands with no secure words. On 128_2v the last line reads 'in dem Drey vnnd d[..]ſten Jaren(?)': the word check found that the letters '-reiſſig-' cannot be seen under a blot, so 'thirty-third' is an inference from 'drey vnnd' followed by a tens word in d-, not a word read whole. The century, the feast and the weekday are not read on the leaf; they come only from the modern pencil note on the bottom fold, 'Mantag vor Thome Apostolj vor weichnachten (1533) 15/XII', which converts to 15 Dec 1533. The line above names '[..]ber zu Ca/La..z(?)', a '[Ger]ichtſchreiber(?)' (the place initial reads C to all readers), '[..] Benck(?)', 'sein Brue[der](?) [..] vnnd Caspar(?) [..]ter auf dem D/J?urnen(?)' and 'obgenanter Capp[..](?)'; the word check removed the earlier 'Jorg', 'Lienhart' and 'Ritten', which are not on the image. On 128_1v the closing lines give '[Herr]schafft Tirol', 'Burger(?) zu [..]' and 'vnnd Liphart [..] Insigel(?)', a sealing clause, with no legible date. No outside record was sought, since no party or action could be read. It stays partial at low confidence because both acts are documentary and a date lead and closing formulas survive, but neither the legal action nor the parties are established; UV or multispectral imaging of both text faces would be needed.

identification: Small scrap of a compressed fourteenth-century(?) scholastic hand, in question form, weighing words 'quantum ad vocem', 'quantum ad figuram' and 'quantum ad modum significandi' with the examples 'albo' and 'dulci'; logic (fallacy of figura dictionis, or denominative terms in a Categories commentary) or possibly modistic grammar, not located
note: Both faces keep about 20 lines each, read in bands at letter level with low confidence. Face A gives 'q(uantu)m ad mod(um) sig(nifican)di', 'q(uantu)m ad figura(m) (et) mod(um) sig(nifican)di', 'albo', 'dulci' and 'n(on) cu(m) q(uantu)m ad voce(m) n(ec) q(uantu)m ad mo(dum) sig(nifican)di', where 'quantum' expands a q with a superscript sign; face B gives 'ad a(liu)d d(icitu)r', 'i(n) (com)po(sitio)ne', 'p(er) actio(n)em', 'i(n)t(ra)n(siti)ua(?)', '[a]d voce(m) p(er) mod(um) sig(nifican)di' and, after a red-outlined initial, '... ad cau(sa)m'. The pseudo-Thomas De fallaciis was compared in its chapter on figura dictionis and is not the text; Google Books, Corpus Corporum and CoMMA searches with these formulas and examples found the topic (denominatives in the pseudo-Thomas Summa totius logicae, the genus of the verb in a Paris grammar) but no wording match. The formulas fix a field, not a text, so the record stays unidentified.

[a]d voce(m) p(er) mod(um) sig(nifican)di; a red-outlined initial opens a new section near the foot.
content.remarks: Not identified. The subject is either the fallacy of figura dictionis or denominative terms in a commentary on the Categories; modistic grammar is possible. Not the pseudo-Thomas De fallaciis.

identification: Stams Abbey, Necrologium Stamsense (lost mortuary), 9 and 13-15 Jan., 9-13 and 24 Feb.; ed. MGH Necrologia Germaniae III, pp. 47-59
note: Calendar strips 168-1, 168-7v and 168-11 come from the lost Stams mortuary, whose older entries MGH Necrologia III (1905) prints from Primisser's eighteenth-century copy; the Stams archivist P. M. Grebenc had already identified, cited and transcribed them in 1964-1965 (slips photographed with the record). A research reader collated the strips against page images of the edition at 14-15 Jan., 9-10 Feb., 13 Feb. and 24 Feb., with agreement in wording and order and calendar letters fitting the days; a second reader confirmed 13 Feb. on 168-11v after an independent reading. Differences are spelling (pietantiam, Leibolvungen), red crosses for the edition's 'missa', and a dense layer of later confraternity obits (Neustift, Kremsmünster, St. Mang, Gries, Wilten, Ettal, St. Emmeram, Buxheim; latest seen 1717) absent from the edition. The date of the base hand (the 1532 copy by Johannes Fuscanes rests only on a Primisser note quoted on the typed slip) is not claimed; 168-4v, two cursive scraps and the host-book spine labels are not identified.

identification: Prayers for the sick and papal plenary-indulgence absolutions, Latin with German rubrics: four parchment corner pieces on a cover, with the orations Deus qui humano generi (end) and Virtutum caelestium Deus (feminine forms), two absolutions separated by the rubric 'Das ist aber ain abs[olucion]', and the hour-of-death remission Ego remitto tibi pen[as purgatorii] in the wording of fifteenth-century confessional letters (Tarrenz letter under Paul II; a form under Innocent VIII); probably from a priest's ordo for the sick, s. XV2 (both inferences)
note: The bottom-right piece keeps eight line beginnings: '[cont]ritoru(m) nec n[on]', 's(an)c(t)e m(at)ris ecclesie', '[fil]ii et sp(iritu)s s(an)c(t)i. amen.', red-initial 'Ego remitto tibi pen[as]', '[t]e illi puritati seu st[atui]', '[q]uando babtisatus fuisti', 'ecclesie se extendunt &', '[d]ecesseris remane[at]'. In sequence this follows the absolution of the confessional letter for Tarrenz under Paul II printed by Tinkhauser (1886, p. 507: 'restituo te illi puritati seu statui innocentie ... in quantum claues sancte matris ecclesie se extendunt et possunt, et si in hac infirmitate non decesseris remaneat tibi'), and its first lines follow a form under Innocent VIII printed by Cornaro (1749, p. 396: 'corde contritorum necnon oblitorum. Et restituo te sacramentis sancte matris ecclesie'); both were seen in search snippets only. Against the Tarrenz text the leaf has 'Ego remitto' for 'Remitto' and 'quando' for 'quum', and the Tarrenz snippet lacks 'necnon oblitorum' the lost stretch of each line (about 25 to 35 letters) fits the short Tarrenz wording, not the longer Venetian one with 'claudendo tibi ianuas inferni'. The top-right piece has the orations Deus qui humano generi (end) and Virtutum caelestium Deus with 'famule tue', as in the Gregorian Missa pro infirmis (Wilson, HBS 49, p. 207); the bottom-left piece has a first absolution, the red rubric 'Das ist aber ain abs[olucion]' and a second absolution '[M]isereatur(?) tu[i] / D(omi)n(u)s n(oste)r ih(esu)s / [ab]soluat t[e] ... pōtifi[cis]', neither matched word for word. The formula circulated in many confessional and indulgence letters about 1450-1520, so the match fixes the text type, not one letter; the book, its use and diocese are not identified, a confessor's handbook would fit as well as an ordo for the sick, and the host volume (a pencil note says Ms. 331) and a Brixen Obsequiale were not checked.

fragmentarium.title: Prayers for the sick and absolutions

content.title: Prayers for the sick and papal plenary-indulgence absolutions
content.description: Four corner pieces with the orations Deus qui humano generi (end) and Virtutum caelestium Deus (feminine forms), two absolutions separated by the German rubric 'Das ist aber ain abs[olucion]', and the remission at the hour of death, Ego remitto tibi pen[as purgatorii et restituo t]e illi puritati seu st[atui innocentie].
content.remarks: The hour-of-death remission has the wording of fifteenth-century confessional letters such as the one for Tarrenz under Paul II. Probably from a priest's ordo for the sick; a confessor's handbook would fit as well. The book and its use are not identified.

bibliography: H. A. Wilson, The Gregorian Sacramentary under Charles the Great, HBS 49 (London 1915), p. 207
G. Tinkhauser and L. Rapp, Topographisch-historisch-statistische Beschreibung der Diöcese Brixen (Brixen 1886), p. 507

identification: Index or list of questions with red question numbers (·99·, ·109·, ·111·), possibly to Johannes of Freiburg, Summa confessorum, book III: the ·109· strip fits title 34, qq. 108-109 (satisfaction) and the ·99· strip possibly title 33, qq. 99-101 (absolution from excommunication); not the printed alphabetical tabula in wording; index not identified
note: Four small strips keep 3-5 lines each of short Latin entries, each closed by a red number with the rest of the line blank. Beside ·99· strip 246-3r reads 'qui e.. tu- / posset [..]oluere' and then starts a new entry 'Qual.. debeat [..] ab[so]l..', read with the source in view (a blind reader had 'poſſet(?) ... [.]ebea[.](?) ... abſ[.]l[..](?)', low confidence); beside ·109· strip 246-4r has 'satisfac-' twice and '[..]facere', and a blind reader tentatively read '[.]atiſfa(ci)o(n)es(?)' there among alternatives. These fit book III of the Summa confessorum, where q. 109 of title 34 concerns satisfaction and title 33 has the questions on absolution from excommunication. The wording is not that of the printed tabula (1476 Augsburg edition, entries Absolutio, Satisfactio, Flagellum, Confessio), which Munich, Clm 2684 has in the same words for qq. 110-112; no line collates, the phrase searched was not found in Google Books, MDZ full text or Corpus Corporum, and no other work (Raymund, the Astesana, abridgements) was tested on the page. The strips are not from the same manuscript as F-d7a7, the printed Tabula of the same work.

fragmentarium.title: Index of questions on absolution and satisfaction, with red question numbers

content.title: Index entries with question numbers 99, 109, 111, possibly to Johannes of Freiburg, Summa confessorum, book III
content.description: Four strips (246-1 to 246-4) with 3-5 lines each along one edge; short entries each closed by a red number. 246-3r: [..] qui e.. tu- / posset [..]oluere ex[..] ·99· / [Q]ual.. debeat [..] ab[so]l[..]. 246-4r: [s]atisfac.. ei [..] ·109· / satisfaciend[um] [..]. 246-3v: [..] ·111·. 246-1r is an old paper label (F 228) without manuscript text.
content.remarks: The ·109· entry fits Summa confessorum III.34, qq. 108-109 (satisfaction), and the ·99· entry possibly III.33, qq. 99-101 (absolution). The wording differs from the printed tabula (Augsburg 1476); the index is not identified.

bibliography: Johannes of Freiburg, Summa confessorum (Augsburg: Günther Zainer, 1476), tabula, entries Absolutio and Satisfactio; book III, titles 33 and 34

identification: Group of small parchment scraps and binding remnants with a few cut lines of Latin prose in a small gothic textualis on 259-1 and 259-2; not identified, register (religious or legal) open
note: Of about thirteen scraps and binding remnants only 259-2 (13 cut lines, photographed upside down) and 259-1 (6 lines) carry readable text; the secure words are 'ut dignus', 'sumat fru-', 'testament-', 'filio', 'cessit · Dom-' and 'alio tempore'. One line of 259-2r reads either 'ego benedicam' or 'ego hereditatem' and the next possibly 'ut dignus he[res]', so legal or testamentary prose fits at least as well as religious prose. The one printed hit for 'sumat fructum', a rubric in Gratian's Decretum (C.16 q.7 c.13), was compared in Friedberg's text and does not fit the neighbouring words, and the rest of that question was searched without result. Full-text searches of the Digest and the Decretals, Corpus Corporum, Internet Archive, Google Books and a complete CoMMA pass gave no match.

content.title: Unidentified prose
content.remarks: Line-middles only, on scraps 259-1 and 259-2: 'ut dignus', 'sumat fru-', 'testament-', 'filio', 'cessit · Dom-', 'alio tempore'. Religious or legal register not settled. The other scraps are unread or without usable text.

identification: Paper strip with the last lines of a page on each face in a small 15th-century cursive; face 2 is the end of the note on Idus from the prose commentary on the school grammar Nomina et verba defectiva (catalogued under Johannes de Garlandia), as printed at Hagenau about 1491 and Mainz about 1493; face 1 is grammatical but matches no witness read
note: The three lines of face 2 agree in order with the printed commentary at the lemma Idus: 'quia olim mercatores dividebantur a nundinis que durabant a nonis usque ad ydus. Et dicitur ydus quasi ed[u]s ab edendo quia hii dies apud veteres epularum fuerunt. Unde ista locutio quarto ydus sic intelligitur, id est quarto die ante illum in quo scribitur ydus per se', read on the page image of the Mainz edition and in the page text of two others; the strip has 'Vel ydus' for 'Et dicitur ydus' and 'diem in qua' for 'illum in quo'. The etymologies come from Huguccio, but the printed note, like the strip, omits Huguccio's middle passage and adds the explanation of 'quarto ydus'; the Catholicon entry and Guido de Baysio's Rosarium on D.18 do neither. Face 1 has two clipped lines with grammatical vocabulary (probably 'diuersorum generum', 'de mutu-', 'secunde declinationis') that would suit the following section on vesper, but no sentence of the printed commentary matches it, and the commentary in Freiburg, UB, Hs. 86, f. 40v, is a different one. The record stays partial because only one face is matched and the strip may carry another version of the commentary.

fragmentarium.title: Commentary on Nomina et verba defectiva (attributed to Johannes de Garlandia)

content.title: Commentary on the grammar Nomina et verba defectiva, note on Idus
content.description: Face 2: end of the note on Idus: [quia olim mercatores] diuidebantur a nundinis que durabant a nonis usque ad ydus. Vel ydus quasi edus ab edendo ... quarto ydus ... die ante diem in qua ... Face 1: two clipped lines of grammatical comment, not placed.
content.remarks: Face 2 agrees with the commentary printed with the text at Hagenau about 1491 and Mainz about 1493 (GW M13741). Face 1 matches no witness read; the strip may carry another version of the commentary. The explanation of Idus goes back to Huguccio, Derivationes.

bibliography: Johannes de Garlandia (attributed), Nomina et verba defectiva, with commentary ([Mainz: Peter von Friedberg, about 1493]), GW M13741, lemma Idus

identification: Paper strip with three lines from the middle of a German letter or letter draft in the first person, in a German cursive of the first half of the sixteenth century; sender, addressee, subject and date lost
note: Three lines and the feet of a fourth were read on the image of the written face (canvas 0): 'auff vmb(?) der Bartl(?) geschickt vnd genugsamblich(?) mit d[..]', '[..](?)schreibt(?) / vnd yms(?) ganz heÿm gesetzt / er schickt d[..]' and 'der Vrbar(?)/Vatter(?) an(?) dise(r)?(?) belehnt(?), ich habe auch nit so hoch an[..]'. The word check corrected line 2 from a personal name 'Hanns Hayim' to 'ganz heÿm gesetzt' (left entirely to someone), so the only named person is 'Bartl(?)', for which 'Hartl' is an equal alternative. 'ich habe auch nit so hoch an[..]' and 'er schickt' are secure and show first-person letter prose. The back is blank apart from a modern pencil note 'aus Einband II/6 36 (c. 1534)': the host volume and the date are not read on the leaf and come from that modern note, which records the reported host volume; it dates neither the letter nor the binding. The same binding gave Frg. 39 (F-t8sd), schoolroom waste with German letter-formula drafts, so this may also be a practice or draft letter; the one 39_7v draft hand compared does not match, and the other German hands of Frg. 39 were not compared. No search was run, as no party or action is established.

identification: Two very abraded small pieces in a small cursive-leaning gothic hand with red underlines, paragraph marks and a red lombard; no secure words, genre open
note: The two pieces (about 12 x 7 cm) sit side by side on each canvas. On the right-hand piece the writing is a narrow column of short lines with wide blank margins and one line in larger script near its foot, which suggests a list, table or gloss column; the left-hand piece has red underlines, paragraph marks and a two-line red lombard. All four piece-faces were looked at in enlarged colour or background-flattened crops and give only uncertain letter groups, with no connected span of two secure words. Nothing was searchable, so no search was run; UV or multispectral imaging might recover more.

content.title: Unidentified text
content.remarks: Almost wholly abraded. One piece has a narrow column of short lines with wide margins and a line in larger script near the foot; red underlines, paragraph marks and a two-line lombard. No word is secure; the language is assumed from the abbreviation signs.
